item.title: Kirill Kaprizov's early goal sets tone as Wild handle Kraken
item.description: Kirill Kaprizov scored his NHL-leading 12th goal of the season and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the host Seattle Kraken 5-1 Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kirill Kaprizov scored his NHL-leading 12th goal of the season and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the host Seattle Kraken 5-1 Saturday night. Blake Coleman scored twice, including an empty-netter with 3:36 remaining, while Joel Eriksson Ek added a goal and an assist and Olli Maatta also tallied for the Wild. Minnesota snapped a two-game losing streak and improved to 1-1-1 on its five-game trip, which concludes with stops Sunday at Vancouver and Tuesday at Utah. Goaltender Jesper Wallstedt made 22 saves. Berkly Catton scored for Seattle, which had won its previous two games. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 shots. Kaprizov, who is tied for first in goals with the Oilers' Leon Draisaitl, opened the scoring on a breakaway just 26 seconds into the game. He skated down the left wing before cutting across the low slot and putting a backhander over a sprawling Daccord. Seattle tied the score at 10:13 as Catton lifted a sharp-angled shot from low on the right wing just over Wallstedt's shoulder and inside the near post. The goal came one second after a power play expired. The Wild pulled away with three unanswered goals in the second period. Coleman scored on a breakaway at 2:11 just after he exited the penalty box, beating Daccord with a snap shot low to the glove side. Maatta made it 3-1 at 11:33 with a wrist shot from the left point that found the far upper corner of the net past a screened Daccord. Eriksson Ek added another at 13:00, after Daccord made a save on Matt Boldy's shot from the top of the left faceoff circle. The goalie couldn't quite corral the rebound and Eriksson Ek chipped the puck over Daccord's right shoulder. Kraken forward Jared McCann, the franchise's career scoring leader, didn't play as team officials said he's still being evaluated for a lower-body injury sustained in a 5-3 victory Thursday against Utah. --Field Level Media

item.title: At least 12 injured in a shooting in Tallahassee, Florida
item.description: At least 12 people were injured in a shooting in Tallahassee, Florida, near Florida A&M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium late on Saturday night, the local police department and the university said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 12 people were injured in a shooting in Tallahassee, Florida, near Florida A&M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium late on Saturday night, the local police department and the university said. Police said 11 of the 12 injured sustained gunshot wounds, adding that 6 of the injured were adults and 6 were juveniles. "At this time, at least three of the shooting victims have sustained serious injuries, while nine others are reported to be in stable condition," the Tallahassee Police Department said.

item.title: Dmitri Simashev’s first 2 career goals help Mammoth beat Lightning in OT
item.description: Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting the Utah Mammoth to a 5-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday night in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting the Utah Mammoth to a 5-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday night in Salt Lake City. After Tampa Bay defenseman J.J. Moser and Utah blue-liner Nate Schmidt were stopped on breakaways in the opening 68 seconds of extra time, Simashev -- also on the rear guard -- slipped in a pass from Barrett Hayton at 1:44 for his first career game-winner. Utah also received goals from Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee. Vincent Trocheck had two assists. Mammoth goaltender Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves and earned the secondary assist on Simashev's winner. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg, Brayden Point and Conor Geekie hit the net for Tampa Bay. In the second half of a back-to-back, goalie Dennis Hildeby made 23 saves for the Lightning, who played without captain Victor Hedman. Nikita Kucherov collected an assist for his 1,138th career point, passing Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead. In the opening period, Guentzel was credited with his seventh goal on a shot into traffic at 5:10 that Utah defenseman Mikhail Sergachev inadvertently put in past Vejmelka. Yamamoto knotted it less than two minutes later when he streaked out and sent a puck in on an odd-man rush. The shot clicked off Hildeby's stick for Yamamoto's third tally. However, Holmberg answered with his third marker a little over three minutes later. In a milestone moment, Kucherov dished out the primary assist to Point on the Lightning's second power play for a 3-1 lead. The historic point prompted the entire visiting bench of players to empty onto the ice and surround the Hart Trophy winner in celebration. The Mammoth also scored on their second power play, as Guenther ripped in his fifth marker to leave the first period trailing 3-2. Vejmelka stopped Point on a breakaway at 1:54 of the second period, but Geekie netted at 5:32 for a 4-2 lead that appeared to put the visitors in full control. However, the Central Division-leading Mammoth rallied behind Lee's third tally and the first NHL goal for Simashev less than three minutes apart for a 4-all tie through 40 minutes ahead of a scoreless third period. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nuggets rally from 23 down to force overtime, beat Pelicans
item.description: Jamal Murray had 42 points, Nikola Jokic finished with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the host Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jamal Murray had 42 points, Nikola Jokic finished with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the host Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night. Jokic now has 199 career regular-season triple doubles, second to just-retired Russell Westbrook's 209. Trevon Brazile scored seven of his 17 points in overtime and hit a corner 3-pointer late in the extra period, Christian Braun had 15 points in the game and DeMar DeRozan added 12 points for Denver. Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22, Zion Williamson and Derik Queen contributed 17 each, Saddiq Bey scored 14 and Jeremiah Fears added 10. New Orleans led 124-116 with 1:37 left in the fourth quarter before Jokic and Murray hit 3-pointers and Aaron Gordon's dunk made it a two-point game. Murray tied the game at 126 when he was fouled on a 3-point attempt and made 2-of-3 free throws with 16 seconds left, sending the game to overtime. Jokic's two free throws in the first minute of overtime gave the Nuggets their first lead since the first quarter. His turnaround jumper in the lane made it 130-128. After Bey split a pair of free throws, Brazile drained a 3-pointer for a 133-129 advantage, and Denver closed it out. The Pelicans raced to a 53-30 lead midway through the second quarter, but the Nuggets rallied in the final six minutes to get within 71-57 before Williamson's dunk in the final second made it a 16-point game at half. New Orleans' lead was 19 heading into the fourth, but the Nuggets rallied. With Murray and Jokic on the bench, Denver cut the deficit to 112-101 on Brazile's 3-pointer with 9:04 left, prompting a New Orleans timeout. The Pelicans extended the lead to 16 points at 118-102, but a 9-0 Nuggets run capped by Brazile's putback dunk made it 118-111. The Nuggets played without Julian Strawther (knee sprain) Spencer Jones (hamstring), Cameron Johnson (sprained ankle) and rookie Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist). New Orleans was without center Yves Missi after he suffered a knee bruise in a loss at Utah on Friday night. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brewers erase four-run deficit, take 2-0 World Series lead vs. Rays
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- Rookie Cooper Pratt singled in the go-ahead run to atone for a costly error and the Milwaukee Brewers overcame a four-run deficit behind six scoreless innings from their lockdown bullpen for a 5-4 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday night and a 2-0 lead in the World Series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- Rookie Cooper Pratt singled in the go-ahead run to atone for a costly error and the Milwaukee Brewers overcame a four-run deficit behind six scoreless innings from their lockdown bullpen for a 5-4 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday night and a 2-0 lead in the World Series. The Brewers, who trailed 4-0 in the first inning, took their first lead of Game 2 in the seventh when Brice Turang doubled to open off Tyler Wells (0-2) and advanced on a flyout. Pratt greeted Kevin Kelly with an RBI single to right to put Milwaukee up 5-4. The Rays stranded the tying run at third in the ninth for the second consecutive game. Jonny DeLuca doubled to open the ninth off Aaron Ashby, who got the final two outs in the eighth. Victor Mesa Jr. struck out and DeLuca advanced to third on a groundout, but Yandy Diaz struck out swinging on a 3-2 count. Game 3 of the best-of-seven series is Monday in St. Petersburg, Fla. Only 10 teams have overcome a 2-0 deficit to win the World Series, the last being the New York Yankees in 1996. Brewers starter Logan Henderson allowed four runs (three earned) on three hits in three innings, but the bullpen picked up its eighth win in nine postseason victories. JoJo Romero, Dustin May and DL Hall each followed Henderson with a scoreless inning. Abner Uribe (1-0) got four outs and Ashby finished for his third save. Ashby has not allowed a run in 15 2/3 innings over eight postseason appearances. Sal Frelick tied it at 4-all with a leadoff homer in the sixth off Ian Seymour. Frelick, who had four homers in 339 at-bats during the regular season, lined a 3-2 fastball 408 feet to center for his second career postseason homer. Milwaukee cut its 4-0 deficit in half with two runs in the bottom of the first, then capitalized on an error to pull within 4-3 in the fourth. Milwaukee threatened in the eighth, but Jackson Chourio was out at home trying to score from third on an infield bouncer on a close play that was upheld upon review. The Brewers, whose only other World Series appearance was as the American League representative in a seven-game loss to St. Louis in 1982, also overcame a 4-0 deficit in the NLCS, rallying for a 6-4 victory over the Dodgers in Game 4 to complete the sweep. Pratt's game-opening error contributed to the Rays' four-run first. Diaz continued to second on Pratt's errant throw from short, then scored on Chandler Simpson's one-out single. Simpson stole second and scored on Junior Caminero's RBI single. Liam Hicks followed with his first postseason homer to put the Rays up 4-0. The Brewers bunched four singles for two runs in the bottom half, including RBI singles by William Contreras and Garrett Mitchell. Milwaukee pulled within 4-3 in the fourth. Pratt battled back from an 0-2 count to draw a one-out walk, advanced to third on Frelick's single and scored on first baseman Jonathan Aranda's fielding error. Chourio prevented a run when his perfect throw home from left field nailed Hicks trying to score from second to end the sixth. That play was also upheld after a review. Rays starter Drew Rasmussen, who was 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA in three previous starts this postseason, allowed three runs on six hits in 3 2/3 innings. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Elections législatives en Serbie, l'opposition tente de renverser Vucic
item.description: Les Serbes se rendent aux urnes dimanche alors que les opposants du dirigeant populiste Aleksandar Vucic, qui a accédé au pouvoir en 2014, l'accusent de corruption.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les Serbes se rendent aux urnes dimanche alors que les opposants du dirigeant populiste Aleksandar Vucic, qui a accédé au pouvoir en 2014, l'accusent de corruption. Aleksandar Vucic a démissionné de ses fonctions de président le mois dernier après avoir annoncé la tenue d'élections anticipées, dans une tentative visant à prolonger son emprise sur le pouvoir en se présentant à nouveau au poste de Premier ministre. Les bureaux de vote ouvriront à 07h00 et fermeront à 20h00 (19h00 GMT). Les premiers résultats sont attendus environ deux heures plus tard. Aleksandar Vucic a été confronté à des manifestations anti-corruption déclenchées par l'effondrement, en novembre 2024, du toit de la gare de la ville de Novi Sad, dans le nord du pays, qui a tué 16 personnes. Une victoire de l'opposition estudiantine constituerait un profond bouleversement politique dans ce pays des Balkans comptant quelque 6 millions d'habitants. Elle pourrait également servir de modèle à d'autres mouvements étudiants à travers l'Europe, qui sont descendus dans la rue ces dernières semaines pour protester, parfois violemment, contre la mauvaise qualité de l'enseignement et le manque de perspectives d'avenir. Depuis son accession au pouvoir en 2014, Aleksandar Vucic a supervisé une période de développement économique mais a également dû faire face à un mécontentement croissant face à ce que ses opposants qualifient de corruption et d'autoritarisme. Il bénéficie toutefois du soutien de sa formation, le Parti progressiste serbe, qui l'a désigné comme candidat au poste de Premier ministre.

item.title: Kevin Durant leads balanced attack as Rockets take down Hawks
item.description: Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as the visiting Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-114 on Saturday to improve to 3-0.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as the visiting Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-114 on Saturday to improve to 3-0. The last time Houston opened a season with three straight wins was in 2017-18, when the Rockets went on to post a franchise-record 65 victories and reach the Western Conference finals. Houston extended its winning streak against Atlanta to five games. The teams will meet again Monday in Houston. The Rockets held the high-scoring Hawks, who averaged 130 points while winning their first two games, to a season-low point total. Houston also got 19 points apiece from Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard, who started in place of Fred VanVleet (right knee load management). Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each scored 17 points, with Sengun grabbing 10 rebounds and Thompson collecting 11. Atlanta was led by Jalen Johnson, who fell just shy of a triple-double with 26 points, 16 assists and nine rebounds. Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels scored 18 points apiece, and CJ McCollum added 17. The Rockets capitalized on Atlanta's struggles from beyond the arc. The Hawks made just 5 of 22 3-point attempts in the first half, including 1 of 10 in the second quarter, and finished 13 of 48 (27.1%) from deep. Houston shot 40% (14 of 35) from 3-point range. The Rockets led by as many as 20 points at 108-88 in the fourth quarter, but Atlanta mounted a late rally with a 9-0 run and cut the deficit to five with 37 seconds remaining. Durant sealed the win with two free throws with 19 seconds left. Atlanta scored the game's first seven points, but Houston responded with a 10-1 run to take a 10-8 lead. The Rockets led 30-26 after the first quarter, fueled by 10 points from Atlanta-area native Jabari Smith Jr. Houston continued to build its advantage, leading by as many as 11 points before taking a 59-48 lead into halftime. The game's start time was pushed back 30 minutes to accommodate the Atlanta Dream's WNBA Finals game Saturday afternoon. The later tipoff did not appear to affect Houston, which did not arrive in Atlanta until after 5 a.m. local time. --Field Level Media

item.title: Portuguese police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, make arrests
item.description: Portuguese police cleared a housing protest camp from the centre of Lisbon in the early hours of Sunday, charging demonstrators and making several arrests, with minor injuries reported, though figures were not immediately available.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Portuguese police cleared a housing protest camp from the centre of Lisbon in the early hours of Sunday, charging demonstrators and making several arrests, with minor injuries reported, though figures were not immediately available. Portugal is grappling with one of Europe's most acute home affordability crises, as prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, with young people among the hardest hit. "We have an obligation to fight for what we believe in," said one marcher, Vitor Gomes, 21, a multimedia communications student, adding that housing speculation, wealth concentration and rising inequality made him pessimistic about the future. Shortly after 2 a.m., dozens of officers, some with police dogs, moved in on the camp in Rossio Square, after warning protesters to remove their tents or face their dismantling, and threatening disobedience charges for those who resisted. Protesters had pitched more than 100 tents after Saturday's protest march by thousands along one of the capital's main avenues. Hundreds gathered to protect the encampment after police dismantled a similar camp there on Tuesday. The police action was "completely disproportionate", however, as there had been no public disorder, Left Bloc lawmaker Fabian Figueiredo said before the action. "The worst thing that could happen tonight was having this police force charge hundreds of people who are here peacefully. Why?" asked Figueiredo, who was at the camp. Protesters say soaring rents and higher living costs are squeezing households and turning housing into a growing source of discontent, with young people among those hardest hit. The Bank of Portugal estimates a shortfall of 300,000 homes nationwide, equivalent to Lisbon's entire housing stock. The protesters are demanding that the government scrap a [USN:L6N45M1AX TEXT:"bill"] to make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading, although the far-right Chega party abstained. The protest followed similar demonstrations in Belgium, France, Italy and Spain.

item.title: Trae Young, Wizards hold off Bulls after dominant third quarter
item.description: Trae Young paired 25 points with nine assists and Kyshawn George added 22 points and nine rebounds as the Washington Wizards topped the host Chicago Bulls 124-120 on Saturday to open a three-game road trip.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Trae Young paired 25 points with nine assists and Kyshawn George added 22 points and nine rebounds as the Washington Wizards topped the host Chicago Bulls 124-120 on Saturday to open a three-game road trip. Washington outscored Chicago 40-20 in the third quarter to create separation and led by as many as 21 points down the stretch. Matas Buzelis swished a baseline three for the Bulls to cap a 16-4 run that cut the deficit to three points with 23.3 seconds to go. But Anthony Davis and Young combined to go 6-for-6 from the free-throw line the rest of the way to seal the result. The Wizards connected on 65.2% of their shots (15 of 23) in the third. Davis and George contributed nine points apiece in the quarter, with Young adding seven. Davis (19 points) and Tre Johnson (13) also scored in double figures for Washington, while Justin Champagnie had an 11-point, 14-rebound double-double. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson contributed 30 points and 14 rebounds for his first career double-double. Wilson, the fourth overall selection in the NBA Draft in June, scored 17 points in the first half to help Chicago to a 62-57 lead at the intermission. Wilson showed his athleticism and explosiveness with five first-half dunks. Wilson notched a pair of slams over a 1:07 span late in the second quarter, scoring off a long transition pass from Buddy Hield and on a reverse dunk off a putback. Chicago struggled to find balance and rhythm from the floor in the third quarter while Washington soared. The Bulls shot 30.4% (7 of 23) in the third quarter. A Norman Powell layup put Chicago ahead by three points at the 10:39 mark of the third, but Young tied the game with a trey on the next Washington possession. George's putback layup with 9:50 to go in the quarter gave the Wizards a lead they never relinquished. Buzelis scored 21 points for the Bulls. Powell added 18, Jalen Smith had 14 and Tre Jones 10. Josh Giddey had nine points, 10 assists and eight rebounds. The Bulls sputtered from 3-point range, shooting 27.9% (12 of 43). Washington wasn't much better from distance, making 10 of 33 (30.3%). AJ Dybantsa of Washington, the No. 1 overall selection in the draft, remained out with a sprained left ankle. The win helped the Wizards stop a five-game losing streak against the Bulls. --Field Level Media

item.title: British PM Burnham open to adopting EU free movement, Sunday Times reports
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the door to the country readopting the European Union’s free-movement rules, the Sunday Times reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the door to the country readopting the European Union’s free-movement rules, the Sunday Times reported on Saturday. In an interview with the newspaper, Burnham said the nature of immigration into Britain had been “different” since Brexit, with more foreigners moving permanently rather than returning to their home countries. “I think you have to have a very factual, quite evidence-based debate about this,” he said, making clear that staying out of free movement would not be a red line for talks, the newspaper added.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama, Spurs pull away from short-handed Mavs
item.description: Victor Wembanyama scored 23 points as the visiting San Antonio Spurs earned their first win of the season Saturday by defeating the short-handed Dallas Mavericks 122-106 in the second of a back-to-back for both teams.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Victor Wembanyama scored 23 points as the visiting San Antonio Spurs earned their first win of the season Saturday by defeating the short-handed Dallas Mavericks 122-106 in the second of a back-to-back for both teams. The Mavericks played without stars Cooper Flagg (shoulder) and Kyrie Irving, who was held out for left knee injury management. Flagg sprained his left shoulder in a win at Indiana on Friday and will be reevaluated next week. The Spurs led 77-63 four minutes into the third quarter but the Mavs cut their deficit to three heading to the final period. San Antonio opened the fourth quarter with a 11-3 run that produced a 103-92 edge at the 9:05 mark. From there, it was all Spurs. San Antonio led by 23 down the stretch as the Mavericks ran out of gas. Dylan Harper added 22 points, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle scored 19 each, Julian Champagnie hit for 12 off the bench and Devin Vassell tallied 11 points for San Antonio, which shot 47.5% from the field. Wembanyama also posted seven rebounds and four blocks. Rookie Sergio De Larrea's 21 points led Dallas. Marcus Sasser, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford scored 12 apiece, Zaccharie Risacher had 11 and Naji Marshall contributed 10 as the Mavericks shot 51.1% from the field. Washington's dunk after a Risacher steal with 38 seconds left in the first quarter put Dallas ahead by one. The Spurs' Carter Bryant answered with a dunk to grant San Antonio a 32-31 lead after 12 minutes of play. The Mavericks went up by six after a mid-second-quarter surge capped by Sasser's pullup jumper with 5:23 to play. San Antonio swung back, forging a 14-3 run punctuated by Keldon Johnson's tip-in layup at the 2:08 mark for a 59-54 advantage. San Antonio led 68-60 at the break behind Fox's 15 points, 12 from Wembanyama and 11 by Castle. De Larrea paced the Mavericks with 13 points off the bench, with Washington and Marshall adding 10 each. The Spurs expanded their lead to 14 early in the third before Dallas roared back, scoring 22 of the ensuing 29 points and regaining the lead at 85-84. The game went to the fourth quarter with San Antonio up 92-89 as Castle and Wembanyama hit late threes. --Field Level Media

item.title: ATP roundup: Taylor Fritz to face Lorenzo Musetti in Lyon title match
item.description: Second-seeded Taylor Fritz drilled 15 aces while overwhelming fellow American Tommy Paul 6-3, 7-5 on Saturday to reach the final at the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes in Lyon, France.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Second-seeded Taylor Fritz drilled 15 aces while overwhelming fellow American Tommy Paul 6-3, 7-5 on Saturday to reach the final at the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes in Lyon, France. Fritz also saved all nine break points he faced during the strong semifinal performance against the fourth-seeded Paul. Fritz had a 32-26 edge in winners and both players committed 21 unforced errors. Fritz will next face sixth-seeded Lorenzo Musetti, who defeated fellow Italian and top seed Flavio Cobolli 4-6, 6-2, 7-5 in the other semifinal. Musetti saved four match points in the final set to hold off Cobolli. He committed just 22 unforced errors compared to 36 for Cobolli. Musetti will be chasing his third ATP title. He is 4-3 all-time against Fritz and has won four of the past five meetings. Fritz will be aiming for his 12th career ATP crown. BNP Paribas Fortis European Open Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff recorded 15 aces and outlasted top-seeded Arthur Fils of France 6-4, 6-7 (7), 7-6 (5) to reach the final in Brussels. Fils carded 17 aces and saved 7 of 10 break points but could not stop Struff, who won the final two points of the tiebreaker to win the match. Struff had a 43-42 edge in winners and won 18 of 27 points at the net. Struff next faces Dutchman Tallon Griekspoor, who rallied for a 2-6, 6-3, 7-6 (4) victory over No. 3 Francisco Cerundolo of Argentina. Griekspoor had a 9-3 edge in aces and committed 24 unforced errors, nine fewer than Cerundolo. Griekspoor has won all three previous meetings against Struff. He is looking for his fourth ATP title, while Struff is vying to win his second. Almaty Open Top-seeded Russian Daniil Medvedev advanced to his second straight Almaty Open final Saturday when third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan retired with a knee injury after losing the opening set 6-3. Defending champion Medvedev had a 9-3 edge in aces in the first set as Bublik struggled to move on the court. After the match, Bublik said he injured his knee in his quarterfinal win over Russian Karen Khachanov on Friday and was advised by doctors not to play shortly before the start of Saturday's match. Medvedev will now face Georgian qualifier Nikoloz Basilashvili, who defeated No. 7 Greek Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-3 in his semifinal. Basilashvili had a 35-19 edge in winners while Tsitsipas had an 11-7 advantage in aces. Medvedev won the lone meeting against Basilashvili, winning in the round of 32 in 2022 at Vienna. Medvedev is gunning for his 25th career ATP title while Basilashvili is looking for his sixth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ｆ１＝米国ＧＰ予選、総合優勝目前のアントネッリがＰＰ獲得
item.description: ［オースティン（米テキサス州） ２４日 ロイター］
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［オースティン（米テキサス州）　２４日　ロイター］ -

自動車レースＦ１の今季第１８戦、米国グランプリ（ＧＰ）は２４日、米テキサス州オースティンで予選を行い、総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）がポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。

２番手にはマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）、３番手にはアイザック・ハジャー（フランス）とレッドブル勢が入り、シャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）が４番手、通算７回の総合優勝を誇るルイス・ハミルトン（英国）が５番手とフェラーリ勢が続いた。

同僚アントネッリとは１０２ポイント差の２位につけるジョージ・ラッセル（英国）は６番手だった。

２０歳のアントネッリは２５日の決勝で優勝し、ラッセルが９位以下、さらにハミルトンが５位以下に終わった場合、Ｆ１史上最年少王者となる。

item.title: サッカー＝バレンシア逆転負け、佐藤はベンチ入りも出番なし
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部は２４日、各地で試合を行い、佐藤龍之介が所属するバレンシアはビリャレアルに１─２と逆転負けを喫し、今季２勝目を逃した。

バレンシアは前半３８分にＰＫで先制。しかし追加点が奪えないまま、後半２４分に追い付かれると、同アディショナルタイム６分に逆転ゴールを許した。佐藤はベンチ入りしたものの、最後まで出番はなかった。

アトレチコ・マドリードはフリアン・アルバレスがゴールを挙げ、デポルティボを１─０で下した。エスパニョールはラシンに１─２で敗れ、エルチェはラヨ・バリェカノに３─０で白星を飾った。

１０試合を終えてアトレチコが勝ち点を２５とし、９試合消化の首位バルセロナに同２差とした。バレンシアは開幕からわずか１勝で同６の１９位と苦しんでいる。

item.title: Cavaliers hold off Nets for first win of season
item.description: Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers built a 22-point lead before holding on for a 125-121 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers built a 22-point lead before holding on for a 125-121 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Saturday night. Evan Mobley added 20 points and 10 rebounds, and Jaylon Tyson scored 15 points off the bench in Cleveland's home opener. James Harden collected 12 points, eight rebounds and seven assists as the Cavaliers picked up their first win. Brooklyn, which trailed 104-82 with 9:29 remaining, pulled within 123-121 on Michael Porter Jr.'s 3-pointer with 8.1 seconds left. Porter fouled out on the subsequent possession and Sam Merrill made two free throws for the Cavaliers to put them up four points with 5.2 seconds remaining. Porter finished with 28 points and nine rebounds, Julius Randle had 23 points and Egor Demin scored 15 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter for winless Brooklyn. Demin made four 3-pointers in the fourth and had six assists in the game. Peyton Watson had 11 points in his home debut for the Cavaliers, who squandered a 29-point lead Thursday and lost 114-106 to LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers. Chaney Johnson chipped in 10 points for the Nets. Day'Ron Sharpe posted seven points, eight rebounds and six personal fouls before being ejected after two flagrant fouls -- both on Harden 3-point tries -- to earn an automatic ejection. Demin and Watson also fouled out. The Cavaliers took the largest lead of the first half at 68-54 on a Watson layup heading into the break. Mobley, Allen and Porter each scored 13 points in the first half, and Harden had seven points, six rebounds and five assists. Mario Hezonja buried a 3-pointer as time expired in the first quarter, pushing Cleveland's advantage to 35-30. Mobley and Allen had eight points apiece, while Porter paced the Nets with seven points and four rebounds. Mitchell was struck on the head by Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. in the first quarter, briefly delaying the game while he lay under the basket. Brown, who is on a minutes restriction indefinitely because of a left ankle injury, will not play Sunday at home against the Indiana Pacers. The sixth overall pick "is on a long-term plan to build him up properly (physically)," according to coach Jordi Fernandez. Brooklyn was coming off a 110-103 home loss to the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday. Randle and Porter combined for 59 points and were the only Nets in double figures in that game. --Field Level Media

item.title: ラグビー＝日本協会百周年記念試合、日本は男女ともに敗戦
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 日本ラグビー協会創立１００周年記念試合のリポビタンＤチャレンジカップが２４日、東京・秩父宮ラグビー場で行われ、世界ランキング９位の日本代表は同１０位のフィジー代表に２８─３４で競り負けた。

日本は斎藤直人、ワーナー・ディアンズ、マキシファウルアがトライを奪い、前半を２１─２１で折り返した。後半に勝ち越しトライを決められた後、ディアンズの２トライ目などで追い付いたものの、２本のＰＧで突き放された。

日本は９月に行われたパシフィック・ネーションズカップ決勝では、フィジーを２０─１５で下していた。日本は１１月、国際大会のネーションズ選手権のため英国に遠征し、７日にウェールズ代表、１４日にイングランド代表、２１日にスコットランド代表と対戦する予定。

この日は男女ダブルヘッダーとして行われ、世界ランキング１２位の女子日本代表は同１１位のウェールズ代表に０─１７で敗れた。

item.title: Rosario Central gana a Huracán y lidera la tabla anual argentina
item.description: Rosario Central se puso en lo más alto de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino tras vencer el sábado 2-0 como local a Huracán en la decimocuarta jornadas del Torneo Clausura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rosario Central se puso en lo más alto de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino tras vencer el sábado 2-0 como local a Huracán en la decimocuarta jornadas del Torneo Clausura. Con el triunfo, el equipo llegó a 56 puntos en la tabla general y superó en dos unidades a Boca Juniors y Argentinos Juniors. “Estamos en un momento alegre y se ve dentro de la cancha la buena energía. La idea es pelear, nos están saliendo muy bien las cosas y vamos por todo”, dijo el colombiano Jáminton Campaz a la televisión local. En el Gigante de Arroyito, el local abrió el marcador a los 20 minutos con un cabezazo de Emanuel Coronel tras un centro de Campaz. Ángel Di María marcó el segundo a los 84 minutos, tras una asistencia de Franco Ibarra. Por su parte, San Lorenzo empató sin goles como local ante Newell’s Old Boys y quedó noveno en su zona, fuera de los puestos de clasificación a la postemporada, a dos fechas del final de la fase regular. “El equipo hizo un partido correcto. Tuvimos orden. Lo que nos faltó para ganar fue presencia en el área. Quedan dos finales por delante”, dijo el entrenador de San Lorenzo, Rubén Insua, en conferencia de prensa. En otros partidos del sábado, Defensa y Justicia venció 2-1 a Talleres de Córdoba y Banfield y Lanús igualaron 1-1. El viernes, Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata derrotó 2-0 a Sarmiento, Platense venció 2-1 a Gimnasia de Mendoza y Atlético Tucumán ganó 1-0 a Tigre.

item.title: サッカー＝アストンビラがマンＣ撃破、ＧＫ鈴木が好セーブ連発
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは２４日、各地で試合を行い、ＧＫ鈴木彩艶がフル出場したアストンビラが、開幕から７戦無敗だったマンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）を２─１で下した。

アストンビラは前半６分に相手守備陣のミスを突いてニコラス・ジャクソンが先制弾。後半７分にアーリング・ハーランドのゴールで同点とされたが、その８分後に再びジャクソンが決めて勝ち越した。鈴木は前後半にわたって好セーブを連発。アストンビラはホームのマンＣ戦で４連勝とした。

坂元達裕が先発したコベントリーはフラムに０─１で黒星。坂元は後半４１分までプレーした。

その他、アーセナルはエバートンを２─０で下し、チェルシーはトットナムに０─２で敗れた。

８試合を終えてマンＣとアーセナルが勝ち点２１で並び、得失点差でマンＣが首位。アストンビラは同１１で暫定６位に浮上した。２勝６敗のコベントリーは同６で１９位に後退した。

item.title: ゴルフ＝バミューダ選手権、前日首位の平田は34位に後退
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフのバミューダ選手権は２４日、英領バミューダ、サウサンプトンのポートロイヤルＧＣ（パー７１）で第３ラウンドを行い、前日首位の平田憲聖は通算８アンダーの３４位に後退した。

平田は２バーディー、１ダブルボギー、５ボギーの５オーバー７６とスコアを崩し、大きく順位を落とした。１３位で出た米沢蓮も２オーバー７３と伸ばせず、通算７アンダーの４４位に後退。２アンダー６９で回った金谷拓実らと並んだ。

オースティン・スマザーマン（米国）とシェイマス・パワー（アイルランド）が通算１６アンダーの首位で並んでいる。

item.title: トランプ氏、独ＶＷの工場新設を発表 接戦ジョージア州で支持獲得狙う
item.description:
Bo Erickson David Shepardson
[ペリー（米ジョージア州） ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Bo Erickson　David Shepardson

[ペリー（米ジョージア州） ２４日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２４日、独フォルクスワーゲン傘下のアウディがジョージア州に、約４０億ドルを投じてスポーツタイプ多目的車（ＳＵＶ）を年間２０万台生産する組み立て工場を建設する計画と正式に発表した。中間選挙に向け、有権者に共和党への支持を訴える狙いがある。

同州中部のメイコン近郊ペリーで開催した政治集会で明らかにした。アウディによると、来年着工し２０３０年代初頭に生産を開始予定で、約４５００人の雇用が創出される見込み。同席したデルナー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「米国市場を信じているからこその長期投資だ」と述べた。

ジョージア州では１１月３日の中間選挙に向け連邦上院選と州知事選が大接戦となっており、トランプ大統領は昨年導入した自動車関税が米経済にプラスになっていると訴え支持を得たい考え。共和党の議員からは「関税がなく、常識に即した規制がなく、カリフォルニア州が燃費基準を規制する権限を撤廃していなければ、（今回の工場建設は）決して実現しなかっただろう」（バーニー・モレノ上院議員、オハイオ州選出）などと賛同する声が聞かれた。

一方で、関税が自動車価格を押し上げ、通商政策の不確実性によって自動車メーカーの一部の投資が遅れたとの批判も出ている。

米国市場向けの全車両を欧州またはメキシコから輸入しているアウディは、昨年の自動車関税導入で１２億ユーロ（薬１４億ドル）の打撃を受けた。中国での競争激化も加わり販売台数は２年連続で減少、米国販売も今年これまでに１６％減少している。

item.title: フーシ派のサウジ攻撃続く、一部再開のリヤド空港も標的と警告
item.description: [２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２５日 ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は２４日、サウジアラビアの石油施設や空港を再び攻撃したと発表した。フーシ派の攻撃を受けて閉鎖していたキング・ハリド国際空港の一部発着再開に対しても、引き続き同空港を「軍事目標」と見なしており利用を控えるよう改めて警告した。

フーシ派の軍事報道官は、攻撃では西部ヤンブーにある国営石油会社サウジアラムコの施設やラービグの石油精製所、原油ポンプ施設、東西パイプラインなどを標的にしたと明らかにした。いずれも、紅海沿岸に位置するサウジの主要石油・石油化学拠点。

サウジ側はフーシ派が発射した弾道ミサイル２発を迎撃し、一部の破片はメッカがある地域にも落下したと発表。これに対しフーシ派は聖地メッカとメディナへの攻撃を否定し、作戦は「サウジの石油施設と軍事基地を標的としている」と表明した。

一方、今月上旬にフーシ派の攻撃を受けて以来、閉鎖をしていたキング・ハリド国際空港は２４日夜、２つのターミナルについて発着を２５日から再開すると発表した。その数時間後、フーシ派の報道官は、空港を標的にした軍事作戦を続けるとして、全ての航空会社、空港職員、旅行者に対し利用を控えるよう改めて警告を発した。

item.title: Earthquake of magnitude 6.16 strikes Vanuatu islands, GFZ says
item.description: An earthquake of magnitude 6.16 struck the Vanuatu islands on Sunday, the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An earthquake of magnitude 6.16 struck the Vanuatu islands on Sunday, the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said. The quake struck at a depth of 125 km (78 miles), the agency added.

item.title: Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms
item.description: US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that. Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied to White House renovations. Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Campaigning in Michigan for US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency. "We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government," Obama said. Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats. They hope that bringing him into the race can fire up their supporters for a tight US Senate race in which El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former US representative. The former president obliged the Michigan crowd by playing to Democrats' frequently repeated criticisms of Trump and of Republicans' willingness to go along with him. "We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, on your dime, like this," Obama said. "Never seen a president so intent on selling favors like this ... Now the party seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A Reuters/Ipsos poll in August found that 63% of Americans think the president and his family have [USN:L6N44F13X TEXT:"inappropriately profited"] from cryptocurrency since he returned to the White House last year and that 69% believe his policy decisions are influenced by his private business dealings. Obama also ridiculed the administration's claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters. "Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, where oil goes through to get to the world," Obama said. The former president also accused the Trump administration of emphasizing unimportant matters, sarcastically calling Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth someone "laser-focused on important matters like the jawline and testosterone levels of our troops" and ridiculing White House renovations as tacky. "He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory," Obama said.

item.title: Joel Embiid posts triple-double, 76ers handle Bucks
item.description: Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 127-116 home win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 127-116 home win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Embiid finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for Philadelphia, which rested LeBron James (back/sciatica). James is expected to play Sunday against the Detroit Pistons, while Embiid will rest in the second half of a back-to-back. Tyrese Maxey pitched in with 26 points for the Sixers, while VJ Edgecombe made five 3-pointers as part of a 17-point, 13-rebound performance. While the Sixers are 3-0 on the young season, the Bucks fell to 0-3 despite eight players scoring in double figures. Jaime Jaquez Jr. led Milwaukee with 21 points, while Kel'el Ware had 19 points and 13 rebounds for the visitors. The teams were tied at 82-82 with four minutes left in the third quarter before the Sixers ended the period on a 15-5 push. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Maxey each made a 3-pointer during that surge, which Maxey capped with a tough fadeaway with the quarter winding down. Philadelphia started to pull away early in the fourth. Embiid's jumper gave the hosts a 113-98 lead with about six minutes left. The Sixers still held a comfortable advantage at 117-108 with 3:18 to go before the Bucks rattled off six in a row in just over a minute to make it a three-point game. However, Edgecombe came up with a big offensive rebound on the other end, leading to a 3-pointer by Brown. Then on the next Philadelphia possession, Brown found Caldwell-Pope for a 3-pointer that essentially sealed the outcome. Philadelphia knocked down five 3-pointers in the first quarter -- three by Edgecombe -- en route to a 34-25 lead after 12 minutes. The Sixers struggled to find a rhythm in the second quarter, as they shot just 33.3% from the field (9 of 27). Brown led all scorers with 16 points in the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Adam Fantilli nets OT winner, Blue Jackets edge Golden Knights
item.description: Adam Fantilli scored a power-play goal 59 seconds into overtime to lead the Columbus Blue Jackets to a 2-1 victory over the visiting Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Adam Fantilli scored a power-play goal 59 seconds into overtime to lead the Columbus Blue Jackets to a 2-1 victory over the visiting Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday night. With defenseman Shea Theodore in the penalty box for a holding penalty on Matthew Knies, Fantilli blasted a sharp-angled one-timer from the bottom of the right circle off a Charlie Coyle pass inside the near post and past the left shoulder of Vegas goaltender Carter Hart for the game-winner. It was Fantilli's third goal of the season and snapped a 0-for-22 drought on the power play for the Blue Jackets. It also marked the fifth straight game that the Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal in a contest. Denton Mateychuk also scored a goal and Kent Johnson added two assists for Columbus, which snapped a two-game losing streak and won for just the second time in six games. Cam Talbot finished with 26 saves. Tomas Hertl scored a goal for Vegas and Hart stopped 18 of 20 shots for Vegas, which saw its losing streak extended to a season-high three games. Columbus took a 1-0 lead at the 11:51 mark of the first period when Mateychuk, cutting through the slot, took a pass from Johnson and put a backhander inside the right post for his second goal of the campaign. Vegas, coming off back-to-back 6-2 losses to Tampa Bay and at St. Louis, tied it near the end of the first period when Hertl roofed a rebound of a Braeden Bowman shot from the low slot for his fifth goal. Trevor Connelly was credited with a second assist. That would end the scoring in regulation with Hart and Talbot both making highlight-reel glove saves on close-in shots from near the right post to keep the game even. Hart gloved a shot by Sean Monahan while Talbot stopped Jack Eichel's try. Vegas outshot Columbus 13-5 in the third period, but could not dent the net. The Golden Knights, who had a three-game winning streak against Columbus snapped, played their second straight game without forward Mitch Marner, who remained in Las Vegas for the birth of his child. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ville Koivunen scores OT winner as Penguins rally past Predators
item.description: Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for the ailing Pittsburgh Penguins, who rallied to take down the visiting Nashville Predators 3-2 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for the ailing Pittsburgh Penguins, who rallied to take down the visiting Nashville Predators 3-2 on Saturday night. Connor Dewar and Rickard Rakell also scored for the Penguins, who won their second straight game. Arturs Silovs finished with 24 saves for Pittsburgh, marking the first time the team has won consecutive games since starting the season 2-0. Steven Stamkos scored his fifth of the season, and Jayden Struble notched his first for the Predators, who are now 0-4 in overtime and shootout games. Juuse Saros made a season-high 34 saves, but Rickard Rakell spoiled his bid for a victory by tying the game with 1:06 remaining in regulation. Pittsburgh played without Evgeni Malkin, who missed the game due to an illness. Malkin's longtime teammates, though, made sure the Penguins earned at least a point. With Silovs on the bench for an extra attacker, Sidney Crosby controlled the puck in the left faceoff circle. Instead of shooting, he fed Rakell at the other circle and Rakell buried it before Saros could glide across the crease. Saros had stopped Rakell twice on breakaways earlier in the game, including a short-handed chance for the Pittsburgh forward with less than eight minutes left. Nashville coach Andrew Brunette moved Matthew Wood onto Nashville's top line alongside Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly following Thursday's 6-0 loss at Boston. The trio produced the game's opening goal at 9:24 of the first period when Wood's shot deflected off Stamkos' skate. Pittsburgh capitalized on a Predators turnover to draw even early in the second period. Adam Wilsby's failed clearance behind the net allowed Dewar to tie the game just 18 seconds into the period. It was one of 24 giveaways for Nashville. Struble, acquired from Montreal on Oct. 9 for a second-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft, restored Nashville's lead at 6:40 of the second period. Besides Malkin missing the game, Pittsburgh has six skaters on injured reserve. Egor Chinakhov also missed his second straight game due to a lower-body injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Drake Batherson (3 goals), Senators too strong for Rangers
item.description: Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as the Ottawa Senators topped the visiting New York Rangers 7-4 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as the Ottawa Senators topped the visiting New York Rangers 7-4 on Saturday night. Jake Sanderson tallied one goal and added two assists, while Dylan Cozens scored and chipped in a helper for Ottawa. Teammates Tim Stutzle and Michael Amadio also found the back of the net as the Senators improved to 5-2-0 on home ice this season. Jonas Johansson, making his Senators and season debut, made 24 saves. J.T. Miller and Will Cuylle each scored and added an assist, and Alexis Lafreniere and Pavel Dorofeyev also responded for the Rangers, who are 1-3-1 in their last five. Adam Fox and Noah Laba each added a pair of helpers, and Dylan Garand stopped 17 shots for New York. Trailing 5-3, Dorofeyev got the Rangers to within one, one-timing a Cuylle feed past Johansson for his third goal this season at 15:32 of the third. Amadio scored into an empty net with 1:14 remaining for his third of the season. Batherson completed the hat trick with an empty-netter at 19:48 of the third. Sanderson gave the Senators a 5-3 lead at 13:38 of the third, backhanding the rebound off Ridly Greig's shot for his first of the season. Lafreniere pulled the Rangers to 4-3 with 26 seconds remaining in the second period, snapping home a 2-on-1 feed from Miller for his ninth of the season. Trailing 4-1, New York cut the lead in half as Miller batted home a bouncing puck for his third of the season at 12:54 of the second period. The Senators took a 4-1 lead at 11:21 as Batherson's centering pass directed off of Cozens' skate and past Garand. Cuylle got the Rangers on the board, short-handed, at the midway mark of the second, snapping a Laba feed past Johansson. Batherson added his second of the night to give the Sens a 3-0 lead at 1:47 of the middle frame, putting home the rebound off Cozens' shot. The Senators jumped out to an early 2-0 lead, scoring twice in a 1:06 span of the first period. Ottawa opened the scoring at 5:33 of the first as Batherson snapped a Sanderson feed short-side past Garand. Stutzle doubled the Senators' lead at 6:39, tapping in a cross-ice feed from Fabian Zetterlund. --Field Level Media

item.title: Four-goal third propels surging Maple Leafs past Oilers
item.description: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday. Jack Roslovic recorded a goal and an assist, while Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored and Kirill Marchenko nabbed two assists. For Edmonton, Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard had two helpers each. Anthony Stolarz stopped 30 shots for his fourth victory as Toronto posted its first four-game win streak since January. Tristan Jarry turned away 25 shots for the Oilers, who had won three in a row. Roslovic received credit for Toronto's opening goal in a high-octane opening frame as both teams' injury-riddled blue lines struggled to contain their speedy opponents. Jarry made a pad save to deny Easton Cowan on a 2-on-1 before Roslovic batted the puck towards goal. Oilers defenseman Jake Walman inadvertently chipped the puck into his own net in a desperate attempt to clear it away 14:16 into the period. Roslovic sprung Cowan on another 2-on-1 early in the second period. Cowan played the puck through the legs of Ryan Shea and onto the tape of Matthews, who ripped it into the open cage 5:29 into the period. Fresh off his game-winning goal against the New York Rangers on Thursday, Stecher exchanged passes with Marchenko and fired it past Jarry from the high slot to make it 3-0. Draisaitl finally solved Stolarz during a period of 4-on-4 play, receiving a drop pass from McDavid and floating one through a maze of bodies to make it 3-1 with 56 seconds remaining in the second. Nylander restored Toronto's three-goal lead 14 seconds into its first power play and 5:59 into the third period off a powerful one-timer from the center of the faceoff circle. MacEwen scored his first goal as a Maple Leaf in a bizarre sequence, driving on net and batting in his rebound 13:39 into the period. Draisaitl scored on the power play three minutes later, then Nylander scored an empty-netter with 2:04 remaining. Lettieri followed with his first Toronto goal with 31 seconds left. --Field Level Media

item.title: Election présidentielle en Bulgarie dans un contexte d'attaques en mer Noire
item.description: Les Bulgares sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour une élection présidentielle qui intervient alors que la guerre en Ukraine s'étend au large de la côte bulgare en mer Noire.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les Bulgares sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour une élection présidentielle qui intervient alors que la guerre en Ukraine s'étend au large de la côte bulgare en mer Noire. Les sondages placent la présidente sortante Iliana Iotova, 61 ans, et l'ancien Premier ministre par intérim Andreï Giourov, 50 ans, en tête alors que 27 candidats s'opposent. Bien que la fonction présidentielle soit essentiellement honorifique en Bulgarie, le scrutin de dimanche revêt une importance accrue après une série d'attaques de drones contre des navires marchands en mer Noire, au large de la côte bulgare. Ces attaques, qui ont suscité une condamnation internationale et des inquiétudes quant à une extension de la guerre en Ukraine, ont poussé le gouvernement à solliciter l'aide de ses alliés pour renforcer la sécurité maritime. La Bulgarie s'est abstenue d'accuser directement Moscou d'être à l'origine de ces attaques, mais le Premier ministre Roumen Radev a déclaré que leurs conséquences "profitaient à la Fédération de Russie". Les deux principaux candidats à l'élection présidentielle ont condamné ces attaques, mais leurs positions divergent quant à la guerre dans son ensemble. Andreï Giourov bénéficie du soutien des partis réformistes pro-occidentaux et exprime depuis longtemps son soutien à l'Ukraine. Il a signé un accord de coopération en matière de sécurité avec Kyiv lorsqu'il occupait le poste de Premier ministre par intérim cette année. Iliana Iotova, ancienne vice-présidente, est devenue présidente par intérim en janvier après la démission de Roumen Radev, qui s'était déclaré candidat aux élections législatives, un scrutin qu'il a remporté grâce à un programme considéré par de nombreux analystes politiques comme favorable au Kremlin. Si Iliana Iotova remportait l'élection, elle deviendrait la première femme élue à la présidence en Bulgarie. Les bureaux de vote ouvriront à 07h00 (05h00 GMT) et fermeront à 20h00.

item.title: Bruins tally 4 in the 3rd to edge Sharks, extend unbeaten streak to 8
item.description: The Boston Bruins scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, and edge the visiting San Jose Sharks 6-4 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Boston Bruins scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, and edge the visiting San Jose Sharks 6-4 on Saturday night. David Pastrnak tied former teammate Patrice Bergeron for third on Boston's all-time goals list (427) to kick off the late-game surge. Fraser Minten (game-winner), James Hagens and Casey Mittelstadt all had a goal and an assist, while Marat Khusnutdinov and Will Borgen also lit the lamp for the Bruins, who are 7-0-1 in their last eight games. Boston's Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka each dished out two assists, and Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves. Michael Misa, Kiefer Sherwood, Dmitry Orlov and Will Smith each scored a goal, Jacob Trouba had two assists, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 shots for San Jose, which was on a two-game win streak. Orlov's one-time blast from the center point off an Ivar Stenberg pass gave San Jose its first lead of the night at 3-2 at 4:03 of the third, but two goals in 40 seconds put the Bruins back in front. Pastrnak jumped right out of the box from a tripping penalty and tied the game at 8:27, taking JJ Peterka's feed into the top of the right circle and firing off a wrister past Nedeljkovic's blocker. Hagens gave Boston a 4-3 lead when he followed up Lindholm's chance in front at 9:07. With the Bruins on a four-minute power play, Minten added an insurance marker at 12:00, burying a rebound after Nedeljkovic robbed Peterka. San Jose would not go quietly. Smith made it a one-goal game again with a 4-on-4 goal with 7:33 left in regulation, slotting home Trouba's feed to the right circle after Macklin Celebrini circled the zone with the puck. With 30 seconds to go, Borgen finished into an empty net. Mittelstadt opened the scoring with his 100th career goal only 3:08 into the opening period, finishing off a relentless shift with Lindholm and Hagens by netting a loose puck from outside the right crease. San Jose's power play evened the score at 5:54. Tyler Toffoli's shot from above the right circle was deflected and found the stick of Misa, who slotted it into a virtually open net from the left side. Strong net-front play allowed the Bruins to jump back in front at 8:20 of the second. After Minten found Morgan Geekie between the circles, Khusnutdinov slipped in from the left side and buried a backhand high to Nedeljkovic's glove side. Swayman denied Sherwood's partial short-handed breakaway off a turnover earlier in the period, but could not stop a second as the Sharks made it 2-2 at 13:34. Sherwood broke up Lindholm's pass in the neutral zone and broke in ahead, putting home a top-shelf shot. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alex Tuch scores twice, lifts Capitals past former team Sabres in OT
item.description: Alex Tuch scored his second goal of the game at 3:42 of overtime Saturday to lift the host Washington Capitals to a 4-3 victory over his former team, the Buffalo Sabres.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alex Tuch scored his second goal of the game at 3:42 of overtime Saturday to lift the host Washington Capitals to a 4-3 victory over his former team, the Buffalo Sabres. Tuch, acquired by Washington in a sign-and-trade deal with Buffalo in June, was in the slot to take a pass from Dylan Strome behind the net and beat a screened Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen inside the left post. Strome also scored twice, and Charlie Lindgren made 18 saves for the Capitals. Jack Quinn, Josh Doan and Noah Ostlund scored for the Sabres. Luukkonen made 30 saves. Quinn opened the scoring at 6:27 of the first period, taking a pass from Olen Zellweger along the half wall, moving through the circle to the net and lifting it short side over Lindgren. Doan made it 2-0 at 10:36. Ryan McLeod intercepted the puck in the corner and quickly fed an uncovered Doan, who fired a snapshot that beat Lindgren blocker side. Tuch cut Buffalo's lead to 2-1 at 16:10 of the first period when his centering pass from the right corner deflected off former teammate Tage Thompson's stick and into the net. Strome pulled the hosts even early in the second period. Jakob Chychrun's point shot deflected off Kyrou's stick on the way to the net, landing in front where Strome collected it and backhanded it past Luukkonen at 2:59. He then gave the Capitals their first lead of the game at 17:24. With Ostlund on his back, Justin Sourdif maintained possession behind the net before feeding Strome for a quick shot from the doorstep to make it 3-2. Ostlund tied it 3-3 at 2:20 of the third period. Owen Power fed an open Ostlund at the bottom of the right circle, and Ostlund's centering feed went off Kyrou's skate in front. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alpine F1 team defends Colapinto after Clarkson comments
item.description: The Alpine Formula One team issued a statement in support of driver Franco Colapinto on Saturday after TV celebrity Jeremy Clarkson joked that he would give him a grid penalty just for being Argentine.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: The Alpine Formula One team issued a statement in support of driver Franco Colapinto on Saturday after TV celebrity Jeremy Clarkson joked that he would give him a grid penalty just for being Argentine. Clarkson, famed for presenting British motoring programmes "Top Gear" and Amazon's "The Grand Tour" as well as the farming hit "Clarkson's Farm," made his comments in an interview with Sky Sports television ahead of the US Grand Prix. Colapinto has a 10-place grid penalty for Sunday's race at the Circuit of the Americas as a result of power unit component changes. "Franco's got a grid penalty for being Argentinian," said Clarkson, a guest of Alpine in Austin. "Probably. Well, I'd give him one for that. "That's just because of what happened when we went there," he added. Clarkson went to Argentina's Patagonia with Top Gear in 2014 in a controversial episode that triggered protests after he drove a car with a registration number that some saw as a reference to the 1982 war over the Falkland Islands that Argentina claims sovereignty over and knows as Las Malvinas. "We're aware of the comments made in a recent TV interview from a guest of the team in Austin," Renault-owned Alpine said, without mentioning Clarkson. "We would like to reiterate that these are personal views and do not align with the team's values of promoting kindness and respect. Franco is our driver and has our full support." Colapinto has a legion of Argentine fans and has had to repeatedly issue statements calling for restraint after rivals and even his own teammates received online abuse. The Argentine said in Austin earlier in the week that the bad comments had "crossed a few lines lately" and said his mechanics and engineers had been targeted by some supporters seeking blame for race incidents. "My mechanics got a lot of hate, my engineer, people from my team that want me to do well and help me perform," he said. "And I'm working with daily getting these kind of messages." Colapinto's manager Jamie Campbell-Walter posted on X that "Jeremy Clarkson’s comments about Franco’s nationality were completely unacceptable. There is no place for remarks like this in Formula One, regardless of who makes them or whether they are intended as a joke. "We have worked hard to promote respect and put an end to hostility and abuse. That respect must go both ways. We cannot ask anyone to behave responsibly while accepting comments like these from prominent figures visiting our sport."

item.title: Pyotr Kochetkov, Hurricanes blank Blues to finish road trip
item.description: Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves to lead the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes to a 4-0 road victory over the St. Louis Blues on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves to lead the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes to a 4-0 road victory over the St. Louis Blues on Saturday. Sean Walker, Jesperi Kotkaniemi, Logan Stankoven, and Nikolaj Ehlers all lit the lamp as the Hurricanes closed out their five-game road trip with a victory. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis each picked up a pair of assists, while Joel Hofer finished with 35 saves in the losing effort. Connor McMichael picked off a pass and came down on a breakaway 1:30 into the middle frame, but Kochetkov shut down the opportunity with a glove save. The Hurricanes stormed down on an odd-man rush, but Hofer shut the door as he stopped Walker's shot and then Ehlers sent his rebound chance wide of the net just over four minutes into the second. Walker got his revenge less than a minute later as he took a pass from Jackson Blake and fired it past Hofer to tally the Hurricanes' first goal of the night on their 20th shot. Kotkaniemi swiftly doubled up their advantage as 20 seconds later he received a slick pass from Jordan Martinook and found the back of the net. Moments after the Blues failed to capitalize on their first power play of the contest, Jarvis sprung Stankoven on a breakaway and he fired it short side past Hofer to make it 3-0 with 6:25 left in the second. Kochetkov was tested early in the third, but once again he had the answer as he denied both Aleksanteri Kaskimaki and Dalibor Dvorsky under two minutes into the period. Ehlers made it 4-0 with 15:30 remaining in the third with a power-play marker. With the Blues' defenders scrambling around, Aho spotted Ehlers open and the Danish forward sent it into the empty cage for his fourth goal of the season. Stankoven had a chance to bury his second of the night off a turnover, but Hofer stoned him with the glove with 12:33 left in the third period. Each team was assessed only one minor penalty in the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Broncos activate LB Jonathon Cooper (arrest) from exempt list
item.description: The Denver Broncos activated edge rusher Jonathon Cooper ahead of Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Denver Broncos activated edge rusher Jonathon Cooper ahead of Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals. Cooper, 28, spent the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner's exempt list. During the offseason, he was arrested twice in June. He faces multiple charges, including felony second-degree assault by strangulation, and is set to stand trial in March. Cooper posted 27 total sacks over the last three seasons with the Broncos, including eight sacks in 2025. He also posted 50 combined tackles and four passes defended last season. Without Cooper, the Broncos' pass rush has still been very effective; Denver (4-2) is tied for fourth in the NFL in sacks (18). Zach Allen is leading the way with 4.5 sacks, while Nik Bonitto is not far behind at 3.5 sacks. Denver also activated running back Jonah Coleman and, in corresponding moves, placed running back Tyler Badie and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss on injured reserve. The Broncos also elevated safety Taylor Rapp and defensive back Sean Fresch Jr. from the practice squad to the active roster. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brésil-Lula et Bolsonaro mobilisent leurs partisans à la veille du second tour de la présidentielle
item.description: Le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro ont clôturé samedi leur campagne en vue du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, en mobilisant leurs partisans et en lançant un dernier appel aux électeurs indécis.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso, Sebastian Rocandio, Lais Morais
item.content:encoded: Le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro ont clôturé samedi leur campagne en vue du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, en mobilisant leurs partisans et en lançant un dernier appel aux électeurs indécis. En amont du scrutin de dimanche, les deux candidats sont au coude à coude dans les sondages, après que le sénateur de droite a remporté le premier tour du scrutin au début du mois. Un sondage CNT/MDA donnait au fils de l'ancien dirigeant d'extrême droite Jair Bolsonaro une avance de 1,3 point sur son adversaire. Lula, qui brigue un quatrième mandat non consécutif, a entamé sa dernière journée de campagne par une marche le long de la plage de Copacabana à Rio de Janeiro. "Nous allons remporter l'élection pour une raison simple: il est vrai que le peuple veut du changement, (mais) il veut aller de l'avant. Il ne veut pas revenir en arrière", a déclaré Lula aux journalistes avant le rassemblement. Plus tard, le président sortant a mené une autre marche à São Paulo. "C'est tellement enthousiasmant de voir tout le monde ici. C'est le genre d'énergie dont nous avons besoin pour le Brésil. Le Brésil est à nous", a déclaré Gisele Passos, une femme d'affaires de 61 ans présente au rassemblement de São Paulo. BOLSONARO FAIT CAMPAGNE DANS UN ETAT CLÉ Flavio Bolsonaro, quant à lui, s'est joint à un cortège de motos à Belo Horizonte, la capitale du Minas Gerais, un Etat clé de la campagne électorale. Aucun candidat n'a remporté une élection présidentielle sans s'imposer dans le Minas Gerais depuis les années 1980. Flavio Bolsonaro devançait Lula d'environ 5 points de pourcentage dans cet Etat lors du premier tour de scrutin. "Le moment est presque venu. Il ne reste que quelques heures avant que nous ne façonnions l'avenir de notre nation pour les 30 ou 40 prochaines années", a-t-il dit dans une vidéo publiée sur les réseaux sociaux. Flavio Bolsonaro a ensuite participé à un défilé dans son l'Etat de Rio de Janeiro, dont il est originaire et qu'il représente au Sénat depuis 2019.

item.title: Serbia votes as students seek to unseat Vucic in snap election
item.description: Serbia votes on Sunday as a mass student protest movement seeks to unseat long-time populist leader Aleksandar Vucic who has held power first as prime minister and then as president for more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Ivana Sekularac, Edward Mcallister
item.content:encoded: Serbia votes on Sunday as a mass student protest movement seeks to unseat long-time populist leader Aleksandar Vucic who has held power first as prime minister and then as president for more than a decade. The snap parliamentary elections, called by Vucic in September, come after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024. The students have since [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"gained widespread support"]. Polling stations open at 7 a.m. and close at 8 p.m. (1900 GMT) with first indications of results expected around two hours later. A student victory would be a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the [USN:L1N40V01B TEXT:"defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban"] in April. It also potentially offers a blueprint for other student movements across Europe, which have [USN:L6N464038 TEXT:"taken to the streets"] in recent weeks to protest, [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"in some cases violently"], against poor education standards and a lack of prospects. But Vucic, who resigned as president to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia from economic obscurity and orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation including new highways, railways, schools and hospitals. OPINION POLLS PREDICT TIGHT RACE Domestically, Vucic has pledged higher pensions and public sector salaries, investment in state healthcare and subsidies for young couples. On the international stage, he has balanced closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union. The students' domestic agenda aims to root out graft and improve schooling, but they have been quieter on their international ambitions. Their list of 250 largely unknown candidates includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic. Opinion polls predict a tight race. In an Ipsos poll published on Thursday, Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) is seen leading with 47% of votes versus 40% for the students. But other polls have put the students in the lead. "The Serbian election is shaping up to be a watershed moment for the country as the Student List mounts the biggest challenge against Vucic yet," said Mario Bikarski, senior Europe analyst at risk consultancy Verisk Maplecroft. STUDENT PROTESTS INCREASE PRESSURE ON VUCIC The railway station canopy collapse occurred along a line being built to link Belgrade with the Hungarian capital Budapest, a project championed by Vucic but which protesters see as an emblem of government corruption turned deadly. Within months, the student-led street protests had become the biggest in a generation, calling for Vucic to step down. Rights groups and activists say [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"repression has worsened"] in the period since. Bogdan Pavkovic was one of thousands in central Belgrade for a final student rally on Thursday. He said he wants to change "this awful, horrendous system which cheats on us, which spies on us, which beats us." Vucic's office and the Interior Ministry did not respond to requests for comment. Vucic and the SNS have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents. He says the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students dismiss. "This has been one of the most difficult but the most emotional campaigns," Vucic told his supporters on Thursday. "We stood against those who wanted to destroy Serbia." RELATIONS SOUR WITH EU Relations with the EU have frayed as the bloc has become increasingly frustrated with a lack of reforms over the judiciary, rule of law and corruption. In a report this month after a visit to Serbia, a delegation from rights body the Council of Europe noted the "hostile and aggressive rhetoric" against opponents. And in September, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the [USN:L1N44Z099 TEXT:"huge public funeral"] of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic held in Belgrade, saying it [USN:S8N43A06T TEXT:"contradicted “the values"] underpinning Serbia’s path towards the European Union."

item.title: Brandon Miller scores 34 as Hornets hold off Heat
item.description: Brandon Miller pumped in 34 points and the Charlotte Hornets recovered to beat the visiting Miami Heat 115-110 after a huge lead was wiped out in the fourth quarter Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Miller pumped in 34 points and the Charlotte Hornets recovered to beat the visiting Miami Heat 115-110 after a huge lead was wiped out in the fourth quarter Saturday night. Dennis Schroder added 25 points, Naz Reid scored 23 and Grayson Allen contributed 20, including a crucial four-point play. Miller was the only one of Charlotte's top four scorers who played for the Hornets last season. Davion Mitchell's 22 points and 10 assists paced the Heat, who remained winless through three games despite erasing a 23-point deficit to tie the score at 100. Bam Adebayo's 20 points and eight rebounds gave Miami a lift, Pelle Larsson supplied 15 points, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson each had 14, and Bobby Portis scored 13. The Hornets looked headed for a comfortable win less than 24 hours after a 47-point home-opener loss to the Atlanta Hawks. Still, the Heat erased a 23-point lead with a stunning comeback in the first six minutes of the fourth quarter. Miami opened the fourth quarter with a 10-2 run to cut the lead to 98-85. That run extended to a 25-4 edge as the Heat pulled even at 100-100 with less than six minutes to play. Mitchell provided the final five points of that rally. The Heat never took the lead, however, and Allen converted a four-point play to give Charlotte a 108-104 advantage. Schroder added two free throws before Miami mounted one final push. Mitchell's 3-pointer trimmed the gap to 113-110 with 8.1 seconds left. Allen countered with a pair of free throws. The Heat made 23 of 25 free-throw attempts to help offset 43% shooting from the field. Miller finished 10-for-29 from the field and made 11 of 12 free throws. Reid sank five of Charlotte's 16 baskets from 3-point range and Allen finished with four. Charlotte led 66-58 at halftime, then cranked out a 30-17 edge in the third quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Zach Edey, Grizzlies look to stay unbeaten vs. winless Kings
item.description: Two big men off to fast starts on opposite ends of the floor go head-to-head Sunday night when Zach Edey and the Memphis Grizzlies visit Domantas Sabonis and the Sacramento Kings.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two big men off to fast starts on opposite ends of the floor go head-to-head Sunday night when Zach Edey and the Memphis Grizzlies visit Domantas Sabonis and the Sacramento Kings. Edey drew high praise from Golden State coach Steve Kerr after his 10 rebounds and two blocks contributed to Memphis' 111-108 road win over the Warriors on Friday. The 7-foot-3 center recorded a plus-25 plus/minus, equaling the fifth-best of his three-year NBA career. He also found time for eight points, three assists and a steal. "Give them credit -- they did a great job of defending us," Kerr told the media after watching the Grizzlies hold the Warriors to two points over the final 3:47, as the visitors rallied from a 106-94 deficit. Edey blocked a Stephen Curry 3-point attempt during the run. "I thought Zach, his defense down the stretch, was really good," Kerr continued. "(He made) things difficult for us." Edey had similar numbers -- six points, nine rebounds, two blocks and a plus-19 plus/minus, when the Grizzlies opened the season with a home win over the Utah Jazz on Wednesday. Having watched Golden State attempt to attack his big man in a variety of ways, Memphis coach Tuomas Iisalo came away impressed with how his 305-pounder handled every challenge. "He was on (Graham) Ike. He was on (Draymond) Green. He was on (Gary) Payton (II). I think he was on (Al) Horford," Iisalo noted to reporters after the game. "(He) found a way to impact the game against all of these guys. "He's incredibly athletic. He finds a way within the game to make winning plays." As the Grizzlies attempt to open 3-0 for the first time since 2017, Edey and Sabonis will meet for the third time. The Kings have won on both previous occasions, but Sabonis has been held to an average of just 11.5 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.0 assists. The Sacramento star has been significantly more productive in the Kings' first two games this season. He had 14 points, 18 rebounds and eight assists in an opening road loss to the Los Angeles Clippers, then posted the 69th triple-double of his 11-year career with 27 points, 19 rebounds and 10 assists when Sacramento dropped its home opener to the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday. Sabonis admitted after the game he'd gladly have traded some of his baskets for assists and looks forward to being more of a passer than a shooter in games ahead. "Move the ball," he expressed to the media. "Get me the ball more so I can swing it and get guys open. We're best when we kind of mix it up -- point guard shoots, point guard hits the corner, point guard hits me, then I can make the read. That's where I'm best." The game also pits two of the June draft's top seven selections for the first time as professionals. While Memphis' Cameron Boozer and Sacramento's Darius Acuff Jr. have both experienced individual success, only Boozer has an NBA win to his credit. Boozer played a critical role in the Grizzlies' win at Golden State, hitting a go-ahead shot from in the key with 20.1 seconds remaining to cap a 25-point, 13-rebound performance. Ninety miles up the road, meanwhile, Acuff went for 33 points in the Kings' loss to Portland. --Field Level Media
