item.title: Sydney's new international airport opens to passengers
item.description: Sydney's new A$5.6 billion ($3.94 billion) airport opened to passengers on Sunday after more than a decade of planning, in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said was a milestone for the country's most populous city.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sydney's new A$5.6 billion ($3.94 billion) airport opened to passengers on Sunday after more than a decade of planning, in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said was a milestone for the country's most populous city. The new Western Sydney International Airport in Badgerys Creek, about 60 km (37.3 miles) west of central Sydney, will operate 24 hours a day, giving [USN:L1N42I00H TEXT:"airlines"] access to a fast-growing and ethnically diverse population centre. The current airport, located closer to Sydney's central business district, can host takeoffs and landings only until 11 p.m. and after 6 a.m., limiting airline scheduling options relative to other major Australian cities like Melbourne. "For the first time in more than 50 years, Australia is opening a major new airport. It’s a milestone that has been decades in the making," Albanese said in a statement. "I’m very proud to officially open it," he said. Qantas' (QAN.AX) budget arm Jetstar was due to operate the first outbound flight to the Gold Coast on Sunday, the airport said in a statement. The airport has capacity for more than 80 million passenger movements annually, it said. The start of passenger services comes after cargo flights commenced at the facility in July. Located on a 1,780-hectare (4,398-acre) site purchased by the federal government in the 1980s, the airport was completed in July 2025 after a seven-year build and 15 years of planning. ($1 = 1.4219 Australian dollars)

item.title: Verstappen's advice to Antonelli: Enjoy the ride and celebrate
item.description: Max Verstappen advised Kimi Antonelli to enjoy the ride and get ready to celebrate as the Italian stands on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Max Verstappen advised Kimi Antonelli to enjoy the ride and get ready to celebrate as the Italian stands on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver [USN:L6N46A08G TEXT:"qualified on pole position"] for Sunday's US Grand Prix and could clinch the title with five rounds to spare, according to the current calendar that includes races in the Middle East, at Austin's Circuit of the Americas if he wins and other results go his way. Red Bull's Verstappen, a four-time champion, will be alongside on the front row and fighting for his third successive victory after Malaysia and Singapore. The Dutch driver will not be making it easy for Antonelli but he also recognised that the main battle was over. "He knows what he's doing, so he just needs to try and win the race. If it (the title) doesn't happen here, it will happen next weekend. If it doesn't happen next weekend, it will happen the weekend after," he said, sitting alongside Antonelli in a post-qualifying press conference. "I think it's just been an incredible season, so you have to also just try and enjoy this kind of ride of the last few months that you've been in. "At one point, of course, it's official, and then you can celebrate probably a little bit." Verstappen said Antonelli, who is 102 points clear of teammate and closest rival George Russell, deserved all the success he was having. "He's very consistent, he's putting the performances in when it matters, and once it's finally official that he is world champion, he's definitely a deserving winner," he said. Antonelli said the weekend did feel different, with his first "match point" in the championship, but the goal remained the same. "We still have to do the race tomorrow, still have to try and win, and then, of course, we'll see what happens. But yeah, I feel like I can enjoy it a bit more because obviously I'm in a very good position," he said. The Italian added that his biggest immediate achievement, on a gusty day with a tailwind blowing, had been to keep his car within the track limits. The Italian has regularly fallen foul of stewards and irritated team boss Toto Wolff with his breaches of the limits this season. "One of the keys was not doing any track limits. That was very good for me because I've had a couple of races where I've done track limits in crucial moments, and that kind of put myself in a bad position and under more pressure. So that hasn't been ideal," he told Sky Sports television.

item.title: Jets, Canadiens face off in Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic
item.description: The Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets will take it outdoors when they meet in the Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg on Sunday evening.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets will take it outdoors when they meet in the Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg on Sunday evening. It will be the NHL's 46th outdoor game and 10th played in Canada. "It's my 11th year and I've never played in (an outdoor game), so I'm really excited," Montreal defenseman Mike Matheson said. "My kids are coming, my wife, my parents. It's going to be a lot of fun. I played in one in college. It's such a different atmosphere and it'll be a lot of fun." The Canadiens are coming in hot, having won two of three, most recently toppling the Chicago Blackhawks 4-1 on Friday. "We want to be winning a lot more hockey games and, to do that, you have to be in a good position in the third," Montreal forward Jake Evans said. "Play a mature game." The Habs played their most recent game without one of its most experienced players, captain Nick Suzuki, who will be out 2-4 weeks because of an upper-body injury. Suzuki did not miss a game in the previous five seasons. Evans stepped up in his absence with two goals and an assist against the Blackhawks, and Matheson added an empty-netter after missing the previous four games with a lower-body injury. "With Nick going down, I think everyone felt like they needed to take another step in their game," Evans said. "It wasn't the prettiest win, I don't think. ... I think we played a smarter game and didn't give them too much." The Jets will be playing their first game since three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner (top goaltender) was traded to the New Jersey Devils on Friday in exchange for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws, a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft, a second-round selection in 2029 and prospect Alexander Command, who was selected 12th overall in the most recent draft. Hellebuyck had been suspended by the Jets for failing to report to training camp after requesting a trade over the summer. "It certainly hasn't been fun, there's no question about it, but at the end of the day, Connor made his choice," Winnipeg general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said on Saturday. "As an organization, we had to act accordingly, and we did." Hellebuyck was introduced to the New Jersey media on Saturday and the 2024-25 NHL MVP brought up Sunday's outdoor game. "There's a lot I need to say, but (the Jets) have the Heritage game coming up," Hellebuyck said. "Out of respect for them and the celebration of hockey, I'm going to postpone that. I hope they know I care about them." Winnipeg has lost four in a row, most recently dropping a 3-2 overtime decision against the Dallas Stars on Thursday. Jets coach Scott Arniel said the most recent performance was an improvement over their 2-1 loss to the St. Louis Blues on the front end of the two-game trip on Tuesday. "We did a lot of better things," Arniel said. "Just, still, some things we got to work on." The Jets also lost some depth on defense when Jack St. Ivany was claimed off waivers by the Washington Capitals on Saturday. --Field Level Media

item.title: ゴルフ＝ＢＭＷ女子選手権、吉田が首位と4打差の2位浮上
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのＢＭＷ女子選手権は２４日、韓国南西部・海南のパインビーチ・リンクス（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、吉田優利が２位に浮上した。

６位でスタートした吉田は５バーディー、１ボギーの４アンダー６８をマーク。通算１３アンダーの２０３に伸ばし、パク・ミンジ、チェ・ヘジン（ともに韓国）と並んだ。単独首位のユ・ヘラン（韓国）とは４打差。

畑岡奈紗と岩井明愛は通算８アンダーの１９位。吉田と同じ６位で出た岩井千怜は３オーバー７５で回り、通算６アンダーの２６位に後退した。

勝みなみは通算２アンダーの４５位。古江彩佳は通算１アンダーの５４位。原英莉花と竹田麗央は通算２オーバーの７５位となった。

item.title: フィギュア＝ＧＰ第1戦フランス大会、中井亜美が2連覇達成
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - フィギュアスケートのグランプリ（ＧＰ）シリーズ第１戦、フランス大会は２４日、アンジェで競技を行い、女子では中井亜美が合計２１９．７４で逆転優勝。同大会２連覇を果たした。

ショートプログラム（ＳＰ）３位だった中井は、フリーではトリプルアクセル（３回転半ジャンプ）を成功させて１位となった。ＳＰ首位の青木祐奈はフリーでは５位にとどまり、合計２００．６２点の４位。住吉りをんは合計１９０．７０点で６位だった。

男子ＳＰでは、山本草太が７７．０２点で８位。三浦佳生は７２．６７点で９位だった。アダム・シアオイムファ（フランス）が１０２．４６点で首位に立った。

item.title: North Carolina State dismisses coach Dave Doeren
item.description: North Carolina State fired longtime coach Dave Doeren on Saturday, one day after a 31-28 road loss at Stanford.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Carolina State fired longtime coach Dave Doeren on Saturday, one day after a 31-28 road loss at Stanford. Doeren exits NC State as the winningest coach in school history. He was 98-74 since taking over in 2013. The Wolfpack are 3-4 overall and 1-3 in Atlantic Coast Conference play this season. "I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride," Wolfpack athletic director Boo Corrigan said in a news release. "I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role. We wish Dave, Sara and his family the best in the future." Todd Goebbel, NC State running backs coach/special teams coordinator, will serve as interim coach for the rest of the season. The Wolfpack are beginning an immediate national search for their next coach. Doeren, 54, coached NC State to 10 bowl appearances (4-6 record) and recorded four nine-win seasons. The Wolfpack have just one double-digit victory campaign in their history. That came in 2002 when program legend Philip Rivers led NC State to an 11-3 record under coach Chuck Amato, who died Monday at age 80. This season, NC State beat ACC foe Louisville 31-28 at home and sustained conference losses of 34-8 at Virginia and 38-14 to host Wake Forest. The loss to Stanford marked the fifth time the Wolfpack allowed more than 30 points in a game. Stanford scored on touchdown drives of 84, 86 and 90 yards in the first half and 84 in the second in its Friday night win over the NC State. Doeren also went 23-4 in two seasons at Northern Illinois (2011-12) before taking the NC State job. His overall record is 121-78 in 16 seasons. Goebbel's first game is on Oct. 31 when the Wolfpack host Cal. The 50-year-old has been on the NC State staff since 2019. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bulgaria votes for president in wake of deadly Black Sea drone strikes
item.description: Bulgarians vote in presidential elections on Sunday as Russia's war in Ukraine spreads to the waters off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lefkowitz
item.content:encoded: Bulgarians vote in presidential elections on Sunday as Russia's war in Ukraine spreads to the waters off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. Polls place acting President Iliana Iotova, 61, and ex-caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, as leaders in a race of 27 candidates. While the presidency is largely ceremonial, Sunday's vote has taken on added significance after a [USN:L1N45Z06Q TEXT:"series of drone attacks"] on merchant ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast that likely killed some two-dozen international seafarers. The strikes, which sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine, prompted the government to seek allied assistance to bolster maritime security. Bulgaria has stopped short of directly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks, but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome "benefits the Russian Federation". Both leading presidential candidates condemned the strikes, but they differ over the broader war. Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier. "I want Bulgaria to have a voice of its own in Europe. A reliable NATO ally that defends its interests through preparedness, strong diplomacy and a clear position," he said at a rally on Thursday. Iotova, formerly vice president, became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter the parliamentary race, which he won on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket. Radev supports Iotova and they both call for a diplomatic end to the war. A victory for Iotova would make her Bulgaria's first elected female president. "My opponents argue that there must be a war of attrition." she told a rally on Thursday. "The truth is, we are all the ones who are most exhausted." Polls by Alpha Research give Iotova 41% of the vote and Gyurov 28%. If no candidate wins a majority, a runoff vote will be held on November 1. Voting starts at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) and polls close at 8 p.m.

item.title: Víctimas de abusos aprueban acuerdo de 800 millones de dólares con Arquidiócesis de Nueva York
item.description: Los supervivientes de abusos sexuales por parte del clero llegaron a un acuerdo extrajudicial de 800 millones de dólares con la Arquidiócesis de Nueva York, informaron abogados el sábado, para resolver las demandas presentadas por unas 1.300 personas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los supervivientes de abusos sexuales por parte del clero llegaron a un acuerdo extrajudicial de 800 millones de dólares con la Arquidiócesis de Nueva York, informaron abogados el sábado, para resolver las demandas presentadas por unas 1.300 personas. La Arquidiócesis católica de Nueva York aceptó el pago en mayo, uno de los mayores desembolsos en la oleada de demandas por abusos sexuales por parte del clero en Estados Unidos. El bufete Jeff Anderson & Associates, que representa a 300 supervivientes de abusos, lo calificó como "un momento trascendental en la búsqueda de la justicia". Este acuerdo solo es superado por el de 880 millones de dólares alcanzado por la Arquidiócesis de Los Ángeles en 2024. La Iglesia católica ha pagado miles de millones de dólares en acuerdos en Estados Unidos en los últimos años, después de que Nueva York y otros estados aprobaran leyes que permitían temporalmente a las víctimas de abusos sexuales infantiles presentar demandas por delitos cometidos hace décadas. Además del acuerdo de 800 millones de dólares, la arquidiócesis accedió a hacer públicos documentos relacionados con los agresores sexuales dentro de la Iglesia. El acuerdo también permite a los supervivientes interponer demandas contra las aseguradoras de la Iglesia para obtener indemnizaciones adicionales, pero evita que la arquidiócesis se declare en quiebra.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis renew warning against using Riyadh airport
item.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Sunday renewed their warning against using Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, hours after the airport announced it will designate two terminals for flights following a suspension earlier this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Sunday renewed their warning against using Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, hours after the airport announced it will designate two terminals for flights [USN:S8N44X01H TEXT:"following a suspension"] earlier this month. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the airport remained a "military target" and operations targeting the airport will continue, warning all airlines, airport staffers and travellers against using it. Late on Saturday, King Khalid Airport said Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers starting Sunday. Operations in the airport were halted on October 10, following an attack on the airport, claimed by the Houthis, that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 others, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. The suspension of operations was extended two days later. The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war. Saudi Arabia has recently stepped up its military involvement in Yemen, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a government counteroffensive after the Houthis seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

item.title: Abuse survivors approve $800 million settlement with Archdiocese of New York
item.description: Survivors of clergy sexual abuse have agreed to an $800 million settlement with the Archdiocese of New York, lawyers said on Saturday, to resolve claims brought by approximately 1,300 people.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Survivors of clergy sexual abuse have agreed to an $800 million settlement with the Archdiocese of New York, lawyers said on Saturday, to resolve claims brought by approximately 1,300 people. The Catholic Archdiocese of New York [USN:L1N41E0QA TEXT:"agreed to the payment in May"], one of the largest payouts in a wave of lawsuits over clergy sex abuse in the US. Jeff Anderson & Associates, which represents 300 abuse survivors, called it "a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice." The settlement is second only to an $880 million deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024. The Catholic Church has paid billions of dollars in settlements across the US in the past several years, after New York and other states enacted laws that temporarily enabled victims of child sexual abuse to file lawsuits over decades-old crimes. In addition to the $800 million settlement, the archdiocese agreed to release documents pertaining to sexual offenders in the Church. The settlement also allows survivors to litigate against the Church's insurers for additional payouts, but avoids a bankruptcy by the archdiocese.

item.title: Bodies of ambushed Salvadoran soldiers found in Haiti, New York Times reports
item.description: Four bodies handed over to Salvadoran forces on Saturday do not belong to the four soldiers who had been ambushed the previous Sunday outside the capital of Haiti, El Salvador President Nayib Bukele said, contradicting a New York Times report.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Four bodies handed over to Salvadoran forces on Saturday do not belong to the four soldiers who had been ambushed the previous Sunday outside the capital of Haiti, El Salvador President Nayib Bukele said, contradicting a New York Times report. "They are not our men," Bukele said in a post on X, hours after The New York Times reported that the bodies had been found and were believed to be those of the Salvadoran soldiers. The four went missing on Sunday after they jumped from a burning armored vehicle that came under attack on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince while they were returning from a market to their base. Bukele said the four bodies handed over included a child, a man much taller than the Salvadorans and a soldier from another country. He shared photos of a soldier's identification from Chad. The ambush was the first major attack on the Gang Suppression Force, a UN-authorized multinational mission, since it began operations in Haiti this year. The international security mission declined to comment on the matter. Earlier this week, Bukele said gangs were holding the four men and that El Salvador had launched a military operation to bring them back unharmed. Additional Salvadoran troops were later deployed to support search and security operations. No group has publicly claimed responsibility for the attack. Local media have linked the ambush to gangs operating in the area, including powerful armed groups Chen Mechan and 400 Mawozo. A year into its mandate, the GSF has about 2,000 troops on the ground, well below its authorized ceiling of 5,500. An earlier Kenyan-led security effort struggled with chronic shortages of money, equipment and personnel. Haiti's gangs have expanded sharply since the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise, taking control of large parts of Port-au-Prince and displacing 1.4 million to 1.5 million people.

item.title: Los cuerpos hallados en Haití no pertenecen a los soldados salvadoreños emboscados: Bukele
item.description: Los cuatro cuerpos entregados a las fuerzas salvadoreñas el sábado —que inicialmente se creía que correspondían a cuatro soldados emboscados en las afueras de la capital de Haití— no pertenecen a los uniformados desaparecidos, dijo el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los cuatro cuerpos entregados a las fuerzas salvadoreñas el sábado —que inicialmente se creía que correspondían a cuatro soldados emboscados en las afueras de la capital de Haití— no pertenecen a los uniformados desaparecidos, dijo el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele. "No son nuestros hombres", afirmó Bukele en una publicación en X. Previamente, The New York Times había informado el sábado sobre el hallazgo de los cuerpos, señalando que se creía que eran los de los soldados salvadoreños. Los cuatro militares desaparecieron el domingo pasado tras saltar de un vehículo blindado en llamas que fue atacado en las afueras de Puerto Príncipe, mientras regresaban a su base desde un mercado. Bukele indicó que entre los cuatro cuerpos entregados se encontraban un niño, un hombre de una "estatura considerablemente mayor" a la de los soldados salvadoreños, y un militar de otro país; al respecto, compartió fotografías de la identificación de un soldado proveniente de Chad. La emboscada constituye el primer ataque de gran envergadura contra la Fuerza de Supresión de Pandillas —una misión multinacional autorizada por las Naciones Unidas— desde que comenzó sus operaciones en Haití este año. La misión de seguridad internacional declinó hacer comentarios al respecto. A principios de la semana, Bukele había señalado que los cuatro hombres estaban retenidos por pandillas y que El Salvador había puesto en marcha una operación militar para rescatarlos ilesos. Posteriormente, se desplegaron más tropas salvadoreñas para reforzar las labores de búsqueda y seguridad. Ningún grupo ha reivindicado públicamente la autoría del ataque. Medios locales han vinculado la emboscada con pandillas que operan en la zona, entre ellas los poderosos grupos armados "Chen Mechan" y "400 Mawozo". A un año del inicio de su mandato, la Fuerza de Supresión de Pandillas cuenta con unos 2.000 efectivos sobre el terreno, una cifra muy inferior al límite autorizado de 5500. Un esfuerzo de seguridad previo, liderado por Kenia, enfrentó carencias crónicas de fondos, equipamiento y personal. Las pandillas en Haití han extendido su control de manera significativa desde el asesinato del presidente Jovenel Moïse en 2021, apoderándose de amplias zonas de Puerto Príncipe y provocando el desplazamiento de entre 1,4 y 1,5 millones de personas.

item.title: Antonelli logra la pole para el Gran Premio de EEUU con el título de F1 a la vista
item.description: Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, saldrá desde la pole position en un Gran Premio de Estados Unidos que podría convertirlo en el campeón del mundo más joven de la Fórmula 1 si los resultados le son favorables el domingo.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, saldrá desde la pole position en un Gran Premio de Estados Unidos que podría convertirlo en el campeón del mundo más joven de la Fórmula 1 si los resultados le son favorables el domingo. Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, acompañará al italiano de 20 años en la primera fila tras la sesión de clasificación del sábado en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin. Su compañero de equipo, Isack Hadjar, quedó tercero, y Charles Leclerc, de Ferrari, completará la segunda fila. Antonelli cuenta con una ventaja de 102 puntos en el campeonato sobre George Russell, su rival más cercano y compañero de equipo, que se clasificó sexto. Aún quedarán 125 puntos por disputar tras la carrera del domingo. Para hacerse con el título, el italiano tendrá que ganar, mientras que Russell y el siete veces campeón de Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, no deben terminar por encima del noveno y el quinto puesto, respectivamente. Hamilton se clasificó quinto tras marcar el mejor tiempo en la última sesión de entrenamientos. La pole fue la primera de Antonelli desde Bélgica en julio. "Hemos conseguido la pole, así que intentaremos ganar mañana", dijo el italiano en declaraciones al público tras salir del coche. "Max ha estado muy rápido e Isack ha hecho un trabajo increíble, así que no será fácil".

item.title: Packers activate RB Josh Jacobs to play vs. Lions
item.description: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was activated Saturday after missing the first six games while on the commissioner's exempt list and is set to make his season debut on Sunday against the Detroit Lions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was activated Saturday after missing the first six games while on the commissioner's exempt list and is set to make his season debut on Sunday against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs was on the exempt list after pleading no-contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and destruction of property on Sept. 10. The charges were related to an incident with a then-girlfriend on May 23 at Jacobs' home near Green Bay. The NFL removed Jacobs from the exempt list on Monday. Jacobs could still receive further penalties as the NFL has a pending personal-conduct investigation ongoing. Jacobs, 28, addressed his situations with reporters on Wednesday. "I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character," Jacobs said. "I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lot of people that know me in this locker room or that's been around me, I'll let them do that. But for me, man, I'm just trying to come back in here and play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward." Jacobs is in his eighth NFL season and third with the Packers. Last year, he gained 929 yards on 234 carries (4.0 average) with 13 touchdowns. The three-time Pro Bowl honoree led the NFL in rushing yards in 2022 with 1,653 for the Las Vegas Raiders. In 105 career games (104 starts), Jacobs has produced 7,803 yards on 1,840 carries (4.2 average) with 74 touchdowns. Green Bay also signed receiver/returner Coleman Owen from the practice squad, elevated edge rusher Arron Mosby from the practice squad and activated defensive tackle Jordon Riley off the physically unable to perform list. --Field Level Media

item.title: Detenciones en Barcelona tras marchas antisistema en los que alborotadores saquean tiendas, provocan incendios
item.description: Un total de 100 personas fueron detenidas en Barcelona el sábado por la noche después de que manifestantes encapuchados que participaban en una manifestación antisistema saquearan tiendas e incendiaran mobiliario urbano en los alrededores de la céntrica Plaza de Cataluña.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un total de 100 personas fueron detenidas en Barcelona el sábado por la noche después de que manifestantes encapuchados que participaban en una manifestación antisistema saquearan tiendas e incendiaran mobiliario urbano en los alrededores de la céntrica Plaza de Cataluña. Núria Parlon, consejera de Interior de la comunidad autónoma de Cataluña, afirmó que alrededor del 25% de los detenidos eran menores. Añadió que se provocaron más de 30 incendios y que 14 tiendas fueron destrozadas o saqueadas en una zona de la ciudad muy frecuentada por turistas. En publicaciones en redes sociales se convocaba a los manifestantes a un movimiento "contra el sistema". Las publicaciones también utilizaban el lema "Institut Indignats", una traducción del movimiento "Lyceés Indignés", que se empleó para movilizar a los estudiantes que han protestado en Francia en las últimas semanas. Videos difundidos en las redes sociales muestran a personas atrapadas en el interior de tiendas, entre ellas los grandes almacenes El Corte Inglés, después de que se bajaran las persianas para evitar los saqueos. Otras publicaciones mostraban a manifestantes encapuchados y vestidos de negro rompiendo escaparates a patadas y llevándose mercancía, en algunos casos animados por los espectadores en línea.

item.title: Flávio tem 50,8% dos votos válidos e Lula está com 49,2%, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com vantagem numérica para o senador de oposição, mostrou pesquisa Atlas/Bloomberg neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com vantagem numérica para o senador de oposição, mostrou pesquisa Atlas/Bloomberg neste sábado. Flávio tem 50,8% dos votos válidos, quando não são computados os votos brancos, nulos e os indecisos, contra 49,2% de Lula. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 1 ponto percentual para mais ou para menos. Considerando as intenções de voto totais, o senador soma 49,9% contra 48,4% do presidente, segundo a pesquisa deste sábado. No levantamento anterior, no início da semana, o placar era de 49,8% a 47,6% a favor de Flávio. Os que disseram que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou estão indecisos somam 1,7%, ante 2,6%. Para a pesquisa, contratada pela Bloomberg, o instituto AtlasIntel ouviu 4.990 pessoas online entre os dias 18 e 23 de outubro.

item.title: Flávio tem 51% dos votos válidos contra 49% de Lula, mostra pesquisa Quaest
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão empatados tecnicamente na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão empatados tecnicamente na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado. Flávio tem 51% dos votos válidos contra 49% de Lula. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. Nos votos válidos não são computados os brancos, nulos e os indecisos. No primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, Flávio terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Considerando as intenções de voto totais, o senador soma 46% contra 45% do presidente, segundo a pesquisa deste sábado. No levantamento anterior, no meio da semana, o placar era de 45% a 44%. Os que disseram que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum dos dois passaram a 8%, ante 9%, enquanto os indecisos foram a 1%, ante 2%. A Quaest ouviu 3.702 eleitores entre sexta-feira e este sábado.

item.title: A FONDO La campaña del Gobierno de Trump para devolver al poder al clan Bolsonaro en Brasil
item.description: Dos funcionarios del Departamento de Estado de lideraron una campaña para devolver al poder al clan Bolsonaro en Brasil e impulsaron con éxito sanciones destinadas a inclinar los comicios a su favor, dijeron 10 funcionarios y exfuncionarios estadounidenses con conocimiento directo del asunto.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Stargardter
item.content:encoded: Dos funcionarios del Departamento de Estado de lideraron una campaña para devolver al poder al clan Bolsonaro en Brasil e impulsaron con éxito sanciones destinadas a inclinar los comicios a su favor, dijeron 10 funcionarios y exfuncionarios estadounidenses con conocimiento directo del asunto. Su plan se pondrá a prueba el domingo, cuando el senador Flávio Bolsonaro se enfrente al presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en una reñida segunda vuelta. Lula ha advertido a Washington que no vulnere la soberanía de Brasil y ha acusado a su oponente de conspirar con el Gobierno de Trump. Los dos funcionarios eran Darren Beattie, asesor principal para Asuntos del Hemisferio Occidental encargado de supervisar la política respecto a Brasil, y Ricardo Pita, otro asesor ascendido este año a subsecretario adjunto para América del Norte. Los detalles de su campaña para devolver a los Bolsonaro al poder no se habían dado a conocer hasta ahora. Beattie y Pita actuaban con mucha libertad de maniobra para gestionar la relación de Washington con el segundo país más poblado de América, según las fuentes. En los meses previos al inicio de la campaña, indicaron a los diplomáticos estadounidenses en Brasil que la política de Washington consistía en restituir a Jair Bolsonaro como líder del país, pese a que había sido inhabilitado para el cargo por planear un golpe de Estado en 2022, cuando perdió las elecciones presidenciales frente a Lula, afirmaron tres de las fuentes. Después de que Bolsonaro fuera condenado a 27 años de prisión en septiembre de 2025, ambos cambiaron de estrategia para apoyar la candidatura de su hijo Flávio, según las tres fuentes. Beattie y Pita ordenaron al personal de la embajada que no interactuara con otros candidatos conservadores que pudieran suponer un desafío para el senador, afirmaron. Desde el año pasado, ambos han abogado con éxito por medidas punitivas de Washington contra Brasil, diseñadas para debilitar a Lula e impulsar a los Bolsonaro, explicaron las 10 fuentes a Reuters. Entre esas medidas figuraban la designación de bandas brasileñas como grupos terroristas y la imposición de sanciones contra el magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal que encabezó la investigación sobre Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters no pudo determinar hasta qué punto ambos actuaban siguiendo órdenes de la Casa Blanca o del secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio. Trump, un defensor acérrimo de Bolsonaro desde su derrota electoral en 2022, no ha respaldado públicamente a ningún candidato. La Casa Blanca se negó a hacer comentarios y remitió las preguntas al Departamento de Estado. El portavoz del Departamento de Estado, Tommy Pigott, no respondió sobre directrices específicas relacionadas con Beattie y Pita, pero afirmó en un comunicado: "Todas las acciones emprendidas por Estados Unidos contra los narcotraficantes y para proteger la libertad de expresión tienen como objetivo defender los derechos y las vidas del pueblo estadounidense". "El pueblo brasileño tiene derecho a elegir a sus líderes mediante elecciones libres y justas", agregó. La oficina de Lula no respondió a las solicitudes de comentarios. Orna Blum, una de las funcionarias que habló con Reuters sobre la labor de Beattie y Pita, dirigió la oficina del Departamento de Estado para Brasil y el Cono Sur hasta que se jubiló el año pasado debido a su oposición al Gobierno de Trump. Washington "tiene todo el derecho a perseguir sus intereses económicos y estratégicos", afirmó. "Pero cuando los instrumentos de la política exterior se utilizan para presionar a otra democracia sobre el destino judicial de un aliado político, se ha traspasado la línea entre la diplomacia y la intervención política". SANCIONES Beattie es un antiguo redactor de discursos de la Casa Blanca despedido en 2018 tras intervenir en un acto al que asistían nacionalistas blancos. También es el artífice de la "diplomacia de la libertad de expresión", una política defendida por los aliados de Trump que busca castigar a las naciones a las que acusan de censurar el discurso de derecha de estadounidenses, empresas y aliados de derecha a nivel mundial. Estados Unidos ha acusado al juez del STF Alexandre de Moraes de violar los derechos de libertad de expresión al encarcelar a brasileños por publicaciones políticas en redes sociales y al censurar contenidos de empresas estadounidenses de redes sociales. Moraes, que ha argumentado que estaba eliminando de las redes sociales las noticias falsas que socavaban la confianza pública en las instituciones democráticas del país, no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. Pita es uno de los muchos en el círculo de Rubio que ven a Lula como una amenaza para los intereses de Washington en América Latina. Rubio ha sido una figura clave en la agresiva política del Gobierno de Trump en la región, que ha incluido una invasión de Venezuela para derrocar a Nicolás Maduro, un bloqueo petrolero a Cuba y ataques militares contra embarcaciones sospechosas de transportar drogas procedentes de América Latina. Beattie y Pita se sintieron atraídos por la política de derecha de la familia Bolsonaro, su antipatía hacia Lula y la idea de que Jair Bolsonaro fue víctima de abusos por parte del STF de Brasil. Al igual que Trump en 2020, Bolsonaro se negó a reconocer su derrota en las elecciones presidenciales brasileñas de 2022, lo que desencadenó disturbios por parte de sus seguidores, que irrumpieron en edificios gubernamentales. El STF lo condenó en septiembre de 2025 por conspirar para dar un golpe de Estado con el fin de mantenerse en el poder. Antes de la condena, a principios de 2025, los Bolsonaro presionaban agresivamente a Washington para que impusiera sanciones, en virtud de la Ley Magnitsky Global de Responsabilidad en materia de Derechos Humanos, contra Moraes, quien había dirigido las investigaciones penales sobre Jair Bolsonaro. La ley es una norma federal de 2016 que permite a EEUU imponer sanciones a personas extranjeras responsables de abusos contra los derechos humanos o de corrupción grave. Alrededor de abril de 2025, el hijo menor de Jair Bolsonaro, Eduardo, visitó a Beattie en su despacho del Departamento de Estado, según dos antiguos funcionarios estadounidenses. Eduardo Bolsonaro llevaba defendiendo públicamente las sanciones Magnitsky contra Moraes al menos desde 2024, y en marzo de 2025 afirmó que era "prácticamente seguro" que Washington las impondría. Eduardo Bolsonaro no respondió a las solicitudes de comentarios. Beattie llamó a la Oficina de Control de Activos Extranjeros (OFAC) del Tesoro para solicitar que se impusieran sanciones Magnitsky contra Moraes, afirmó un exfuncionario estadounidense, quien destacó que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, cuyo departamento gestiona las sanciones Magnitsky a través de la OFAC, no puso ninguna objeción. Estados Unidos anunció sanciones Magnitsky contra Moraes en julio de 2025, alegando sus presuntas violaciones del derecho a la libertad de expresión al censurar publicaciones antigubernamentales en las redes sociales. Un funcionario del Tesoro afirmó que Bessent y Rubio están "totalmente alineados con la política exterior del Gobierno". DESIGNACIONES La familia Bolsonaro también presionaba para que Washington designara a las principales bandas de Brasil —el Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) y el Comando Vermelho (CV)— como organizaciones terroristas. Creían que dicha medida perjudicaría a Lula, a quien algunos han criticado por no controlar la delincuencia. Eduardo Bolsonaro había entablado amistad con Pita a través de los círculos conservadores estadounidenses, y ambos apoyaban la iniciativa de designar a las bandas como grupos terroristas. En mayo de 2025, Pita se unió a una delegación de Washington que visitó a Jair Bolsonaro en su residencia de Brasilia mientras esperaba su juicio, según comunicados públicos. También formaba parte del grupo David Gamble, el máximo responsable de sanciones del Departamento de Estado en ese momento. De vuelta en Washington, Pita pidió a los responsables de sanciones del Departamento de Estado que estudiaran cómo podrían aplicarse en Brasil las designaciones como organizaciones terroristas, similares a las anunciadas contra los cárteles mexicanos en febrero de 2025, afirmó un exfuncionario. En mayo de 2026 —tras el ascenso de Pita a un puesto que le apartó de los asuntos relacionados con Brasil—, Flávio Bolsonaro se reunió en Washington con Beattie y el subsecretario de Estado Christopher Landau para debatir "la urgencia de designar al PCC y al Comando Vermelho como organizaciones terroristas extranjeras", según una publicación en X del influencer de derecha Paulo Figueiredo que incluía fotos de los asistentes. El Departamento de Estado anunció la designación al día siguiente. Reuters no pudo determinar el alcance de la influencia de Pita o Beattie a la hora de conseguir la decisión final. En julio de 2025, Washington también anunció una serie de medidas adicionales contra Brasil, entre ellas la revocación de los visados de ocho magistrados del STF y la imposición de aranceles del 50% a los productos brasileños, alegando la "persecución" contra Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters no pudo determinar qué papel, si es que hubo alguno, desempeñaron Beattie o Pita en las medidas adicionales. Pero si su intención era socavar a Lula, muchas de ellas resultaron contraproducentes, según analistas políticos de Brasil. Las medidas dirigidas contra el STF no impidieron en absoluto que este siguiera adelante con el juicio a Bolsonaro, mientras que los aranceles impulsaron los índices de popularidad del Gobierno de Lula, señalaron analistas. Las principales empresas estadounidenses y brasileñas que dependen del comercio bilateral —entre ellas el gigante cárnico JBS (JBSS.O) , controlado por los multimillonarios brasileños Wesley y Joesley Batista— también se opusieron a los aranceles, que Washington acabó suavizando. La campaña de Beattie y Pita también sufrió reveses. Sin una explicación oficial por parte del Departamento del Tesoro, Washington retiró al juez Moraes de la lista de sanciones Magnitsky en diciembre, y en marzo Brasil prohibió a Beattie entrar en el país para visitar a Bolsonaro en prisión.

item.title: North Korea's Kim Jong Un returns from China after war memorial visit, state media says
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned to his country by road on Sunday after visiting a historic Korean War memorial in the Chinese border city of Dandong, North Korean state media reported.
item.dc:creator: Cynthia Kim, Joyce Lee
item.content:encoded: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned to his country by road on Sunday after visiting a historic Korean War memorial in the Chinese border city of Dandong, North Korean state media reported. Kim visited the city on Saturday and crossed a newly opened bridge that connects the country to its biggest trading partner, China, which was seen as symbolizing a push by Beijing and Pyongyang to expand trade ties. North Korean state media heavily emphasized the historical weight of the visit, describing the bilateral relationship as an "unbreakable" bond forged during the 1950-1953 conflict. Kim stated during his tour that the North Korean people would "forever remember the glorious years of fighting alongside the Chinese people" and pass down "generational gratitude to the Chinese people who helped our revolution with blood," according to the KCNA. The visit is seen as a renewed [USN:L1N46A01U TEXT:"push"] by China and North Korea to bolster their economic relationship ahead of a trip to the region by US President Donald Trump next month. It also highlights a sophisticated diplomatic balancing act by Pyongyang, which has been deepening [USN:L4N44L021 TEXT:"military ties"] with Moscow in the past two years. Guided by Wang Huning, the fourth-ranking official in the Chinese Communist Party, Kim visited the "Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea" in the border city of Dandong, accompanied by a high-level North Korean delegation that included his sister, Kim Yo Jong, and Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui. Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025 for a military parade, and Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea in June. "Enjoying a bird's-eye view at the middle point of the newly-inaugurated bridge, Comrade Kim Jong Un expressed expectation that the bridge would undoubtedly and correctly fulfill its historic mission of linking the two countries and firmly joining the minds of the peoples of the two countries," KCNA reported. The two Koreas are technically at war after their 1950-53 war ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

item.title: SGA, Thunder hope a new streak starts vs. Clippers
item.description: Oklahoma City Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander will look to start another streak Sunday when the Thunder host the Los Angeles Clippers.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Oklahoma City Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander will look to start another streak Sunday when the Thunder host the Los Angeles Clippers. Gilgeous-Alexander's NBA-record streak of 141 consecutive games with 20 or more points was snapped in Thursday's 96-84 win over Denver. Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 17 points versus the Nuggets, scoring 10 in the fourth quarter to make a run at extending the streak before pulling himself out of the game with 1:24 remaining and a Thunder win out of reach. "I feel like you always treat the game with respect," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "God willing, I have many more games to start on a streak. So, it's not the end of the world." Gilgeous-Alexander doesn't figure to have another streak quite that long. All-time great Wilt Chamberlain previously held the record with 126 consecutive games with 20 or more points. No other player has had a streak of 100 such games. "If you don't play basketball, you probably don't even realize how crazy (the streak) is," Oklahoma City's Jalen Williams said. "Like, people in video games don't do that. ... It's very impressive. I can confidently say that one will be untouched for a while." After a season in which he was limited to just 33 regular-season games due to injury and missed much of the postseason, Williams has had a strong start to this season. He had 21 points on 7-of-15 shooting in Thursday's win. It's early, but the Thunder's defense figures to be one of the NBA's best yet again this season. Through two games, Oklahoma City is holding opponents to just 95.9 points per 100 possessions. The Thunder led the NBA in defensive rating a year ago at 106.5 and points off turnovers with 22.0. The Clippers will need to show plenty of improvement in ball security against the Thunder after committing 26 turnovers in Friday's 125-117 loss to the Lakers. In that loss, Darius Garland had a career-high nine turnovers. Clippers coach Tyronn Lue said Garland needed to be better. "He's the head of the snake, and he has to take care of the basketball, score the basketball, and also get guys involved," Lue said. "Teams are going to throw a lot of different looks at him, so he's got to be ready for it." Sunday's game is the second in a stretch where the Clippers will play four of five games away from home. Los Angeles is averaging 22 turnovers through two games. "We're going to play hard," Lue said. "We're going to scrap to the end. ... We've got to do a better job of taking care of the ball." The Thunder have swept the season series between the teams in each of the last two seasons. The Clippers have lost nine consecutive games in Oklahoma City. Their last road win over the Thunder came in March 2020. An Oklahoma City win could help the Thunder beyond just this year's standings. The Thunder are likely to own the Clippers' first-round pick in the 2027 NBA Draft. Los Angeles remains without Brandon Ingram, Bradley Beal, Max Strus and Yanic Konan Niederhauser. --Field Level Media

item.title: Top 25 roundup: Cincinnati shocks No. 8 Texas Tech; No. 1 Miami rolls
item.description: Cincinnati quarterback JC French IV threw for four touchdowns and Cole Tabb ran for a career-high 173 yards and a score as the host Bearcats posted their biggest upset in nearly 20 years with a 37-24 Big 12 victory over No. 8 Texas Tech.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cincinnati quarterback JC French IV threw for four touchdowns and Cole Tabb ran for a career-high 173 yards and a score as the host Bearcats posted their biggest upset in nearly 20 years with a 37-24 Big 12 victory over No. 8 Texas Tech. After squandering an opportunity to win last weekend at West Virginia, the Bearcats completed a 180-degree turn by dominating the Red Raiders to snap a two-game losing streak. It marked the Bearcats' largest win over a ranked foe since they beat No. 7 Rutgers 30-11 on Nov. 18, 2006. It also served as the fourth win over a Top 10 foe in school history. French, who completed 19 of 30 passes for 172 yards, threw for three touchdowns in the final 7:48 of the first half to turn a 6-3 deficit into a 24-6 halftime lead. He connected with Tabb for a 4-yard score, Malachi Henry for a 5-yard touchdown and Lyviel Waters for 2 yards with five seconds left in the half. Texas Tech tried to rally early in the third. Peyton Morgan picked off French and returned it 53 yards for a touchdown with 8:49 remaining in the quarter to cut the deficit to 24-15. Cincinnati responded with a nine-play, 80-yard drive that French capped with a 17-yard pass to Larenzo Fenner. No. 1 Miami 52, Pittsburgh 23 Malachi Toney caught a school-record 16 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns to lead the Hurricanes to a comfortable Atlantic Coast Conference win at home against the Panthers. Toney finished the first half with 11 catches for 147 yards to secure his sixth career double-digit catch game. The Hurricanes (7-0, 5-0 ACC) won their first game as the nation's top-ranked team since 2002. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah was efficient once again, completing 31 of 37 passes for 387 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. Pitt (5-3, 2-3) dropped its third consecutive game since losing quarterback Mason Heintschel for the season with a torn ACL. Holden Geriner made his second start in Pitt's past three games. He completed 18 of 32 passes for 268 yards and one touchdown. No. 6 Indiana 13, Michigan 6 (OT) Josh Hoover scored on a 4-yard keeper in overtime to lift the Hoosiers to a Big Ten victory over Michigan in Ann Arbor, Mich. Turbo Richard rushed 19 times for 68 yards and Lee Beebe Jr. added 56 yards on 12 carries for Indiana (7-1, 4-1), which had not won at Michigan since 1967. Hoover completed 8 of 18 passes for 81 yards and his first interception of the year while Nico Radicic booted two field goals. Freshman quarterback Tommy Carr hit 20 of 32 passes for 167 yards in his first start for Michigan. JJ Buchanan caught six passes for 57 yards and Trey Butkowski kicked two field goals, including a 26-yarder on the final play of regulation. No. 18 LSU, Auburn 17 Sam Leavitt threw for three touchdowns and ran for a fourth as LSU routed host Auburn for an SEC win. Leavitt completed 32 of 45 for a career-high 387 yards as LSU outgained Auburn 552-271. Jackson Harris caught nine passes for 178 yards and two scores for LSU (6-2, 3-2 SEC), which ended an eight-game losing streak in SEC road games dating to the 2024 season. Byrum Brown passed for 160 yards and rushed for a team-high 21 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries for Auburn (4-3, 2-3), which never led one week after upsetting top-ranked Georgia. No. 23 SMU 59, Cal 20 Kendrick Raphael rushed for 104 yards and two touchdowns against his former team to help the Mustangs pull away from the Golden Bears for an ACC win in Dallas. Raphael, who rushed for 943 yards and 13 touchdowns for Cal last season, also snared a touchdown pass from Kevin Jennings, who completed 16 of 23 attempts for 223 yards and three touchdowns. Christian Rhodes added two short touchdown runs for the Mustangs (6-1, 3-1 ACC), who outscored Cal 42-0 in the second half after trailing by three at halftime. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed 27 of 37 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown for the Golden Bears (3-5, 2-3), who scored first when they moved the ball 65 yards in seven plays on their opening drive. Sagapolutele capped the march with a 10-yard touchdown pass to Chase Hendricks. No. 24 Northwestern 42, Rutgers 14 Aidan Chiles threw three touchdowns and ran for two scores as the Wildcats raced out to a big lead in the first half and rolled to the Big Ten victory in Evanston, Ill. Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) earned its fourth straight win as Chiles completed 19 of 25 passes for 219 yards and added 83 rushing yards. Caleb Komolafe rushed for 150 yards, which included a 33-yard score that put the Wildcats up 28-3 late in the first half. Griffin Wilde added nine catches for 133 yards and a score. Antwan Raymond rushed for a season-high 150 yards and Clay Thevenin added 116 yards for Rutgers (2-5, 1-3), which lost its 46th consecutive game against a ranked opponent. Starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan played just three snaps before getting hurt on a scramble. Backup AJ Surace completed 7 of 18 passes for 64 yards. --Field Level Media

item.title: Arrests in Barcelona after 'anti-system' rioters loot shops, set fires
item.description: A total of 100 people were arrested in Barcelona on Saturday evening after hooded demonstrators who participated in an anti-establishment rally looted shops and set fire to street furniture around the city's central Plaza de Catalunya.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A total of 100 people were arrested in Barcelona on Saturday evening after hooded demonstrators who participated in an anti-establishment rally looted shops and set fire to street furniture around the city's central Plaza de Catalunya. Núria Parlon, the interior minister for the Spanish region of Catalonia, said around 25% of those arrested were minors. More than 30 fires were set and 14 stores vandalised or looted in a part of town popular with tourists and weekend shoppers, she added. Demonstrators were called in social media posts to a movement "against the system." The posts also used the slogan "Institut Indignats", a translation of the movement "Lyceés Indignés" which was used to rally students who have protested in France in recent weeks. In English, the phrases translate as "Indignant High School Student." Social media videos show people trapped inside shops including department store El Corte Ingles after shutters were lowered to prevent looting. Other posts showed hooded demonstrators dressed in black kicking in shop windows and making off with goods, in some cases encouraged by online viewers. Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni said acts of vandalism in the city "will not go unpunished", including legal consequences for the guardians of any minors involved.

item.title: Antonelli on pole for US Grand Prix that could secure F1 title
item.description: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli will start on pole position for a US Grand Prix that could make him Formula One's youngest world champion, and Italy's first since 1953, if results go his way on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli will start on pole position for a US Grand Prix that could make him Formula One's youngest world champion, and Italy's first since 1953, if results go his way on Sunday. Red Bull's Max Verstappen joined the 20-year-old on the front row after Saturday's qualifying at Austin's Circuit of the Americas with teammate Isack Hadjar qualifying third and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc completing the second row. Antonelli has a 102-point lead in the championship over closest rival and teammate George Russell, who qualified only sixth, with 125 points still to be won after Sunday's 56 lap race. To take the title in Texas, the Italian will need to win with Russell and Ferrari's seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton finishing no higher than ninth or fifth respectively. Otherwise, his next opportunity will be in Mexico next weekend. Hamilton qualified fifth after setting the fastest time in final practice but was then unable to continue the momentum into qualifying. GOOD TO BE BACK The unexpected pole was Antonelli's first since Belgium in July, and seventh so far this season, and he found the speed just when he needed it. "It feels good to be back," he said over the team radio after a gusty session. "We got pole, so we will try to win tomorrow," he added in comments to the crowd after stepping out of the car. "Max has been very quick and Isack did an incredible job, so it won't be easy. We will try to get a good start and hopefully we lead into Turn One, then set the pace, even though it will be very tight." Antonelli set his time of one minute 34.035 with his first flying lap of the final phase, leaving him 0.179 quicker than Verstappen who won last year in Austin from pole and has also won the last two races this season in Malaysia and Singapore. "There were no mistakes but just no grip and (the car) started to slide a lot and then the final lap, you can see that it's not really happening with the tail wind in places," said Verstappen. "So you try to push a bit more, you hit the bump wrong and the car is like a kangaroo and you have a massive slide, so you know the lap is over." Hadjar also said he had a tailwind, costing him time and a possible shot at pole. Russell hoped strategy could get him back in contention on Sunday but recognised Antonelli had landed another telling blow. "Qualifying was looking OK to be honest until we got to Q3," said the Briton. "I just did two bad laps and that's why we were where we were. Kimi did a great job." Leclerc recalled that he won in 2024 from fourth on the grid and hoped he might repeat the feat, blaming tyre temperatures for his Saturday problems. "There was a bit more cloud in Q3. We lost one or two degrees of track temp and, for us, it was night and day different and already from the out lap I felt I was having lots of difficulties," said the Monegasque. McLaren's Oscar Piastri qualified seventh, one place ahead of reigning world champion teammate Lando Norris, and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad was ninth fastest but has a five-place grid penalty for a power unit component change. That will lift teammate Liam Lawson to ninth with Alpine's Pierre Gasly also moving up to complete the top 10. Lawson did not take part in the final phase, preferring to save tyres for Sunday and knowing he was unlikely to get much higher up the grid.
