item.title: Devils limit Kings to 13 shots, register third consecutive win
item.description: Arseny Gritsyuk scored for the fifth straight game to help the New Jersey Devils seal a 3-1 win against Los Angeles Kings on Saturday afternoon in Newark, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Arseny Gritsyuk scored for the fifth straight game to help the New Jersey Devils seal a 3-1 win against Los Angeles Kings on Saturday afternoon in Newark, N.J. Anthony Mantha and Brett Pesce also scored, and Jake Allen made 12 saves for New Jersey, which has won five of the past six. Scott Laughton scored and Anton Forsberg made 23 saves for the Kings, who had won two in a row following a 0-4-2 start to the season. Pesce gave the Devils a 2-1 lead at 8:08 of the third period. The veteran defenseman had the time and space to hold the puck and wait for Kings forward Andre Lee to slide by before scoring with a wrist shot from above the right hash marks. The Kings briefly thought they tied it with 4:36 left on a deflection by Trevor Moore, but it was quickly ruled on the ice that he had used a high stick and confirmed on review. Gritsyuk scored into an empty net with 1:05 left for a 3-1 lead. Forsberg helped keep the game scoreless by making back-to-back pad saves without his goal stick at 12:03 and 12:12 of the second period. Shortly afterward, the Devils were on a power play when Kings forward Joel Armia stuck out his stick blade and prevented the puck from sliding over the goal line after it got behind Forsberg. Laughton came out of the box on the same penalty and stayed on the ice before receiving an Adrian Kempe pass from below the goal line and scoring via a one-timer for a 1-0 lead at 15:57 of the second. Mantha tied it 1-1 at 18:43 of the second. Jesper Boqvist circled behind the Los Angeles net before passing the puck out to Mantha at the top of the left circle. He stopped the puck with his skate, skated into the circle and avoided two defenders before snapping a shot past Forsberg. The Kings were outshot 14-3 in the second period after both teams combined for just nine shots in the first period. --Field Level Media

item.title: Texans WR Tank Dell activated to return after 22-month recovery
item.description: The Texans formally activated Tank Dell to the active roster on Saturday and the receiver is set to play for the first time in 22 months when Houston hosts the New York Giants on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Texans formally activated Tank Dell to the active roster on Saturday and the receiver is set to play for the first time in 22 months when Houston hosts the New York Giants on Sunday. Dell sustained a serious left knee injury in Week 16 of the 2024 season against the Kansas City Chiefs and missed all of last season. Dell was injured while making a 30-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter against the Chiefs on Dec. 21, 2024. He dislocated his kneecap, tore three ligaments (ACL, MCL, LCL) and tore the meniscus. Dell said earlier this week that he's aware people are wondering how his knee will hold up. "I know it's a lot of questions, like, 'How he gonna look when he gets tackled?'" Dell said. "I don't care about none of that. I'm ready to get tackled. I'm gonna be joyful. Y'all gonna see the passion I have after I had that first catch." Dell, who turns 27 on Oct. 29, started this season on injured reserve. The Texans opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 6, and Dell began practicing the following day. Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said earlier this week that Dell's explosiveness remains impressive. "He's still quick as ever," Ryans said. "Ask our defenders who was covering him the past couple weeks, he's been putting us in some tough matchups and practice the past two weeks. I expect him to go out on Sunday and do the same thing. Really stress defenders and that's what Tank is going to do with his speed, his playmaking ability." Dell made 98 catches for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns in 25 games (18 starts) over his first two NFL seasons. He was a third-round pick in 2023 out of Houston. The Texans also elevated cornerback Bryce Hall and linebacker Kenneth Murray from the practice squad for Sunday's game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vídeo omite trecho de live em que Bolsonaro defende remédios sem eficácia contra Covid-19
item.description: Um vídeo em que o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro imita uma pessoa com falta de ar e defende o "tratamento inicial" para a Covid-19 omite os trechos em que o político citou o uso de remédios sem eficácia comprovada contra a doença como parte do tal "tratamento".
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo em que o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro imita uma pessoa com falta de ar e defende o "tratamento inicial" para a Covid-19 omite os trechos em que o político citou o uso de remédios sem eficácia comprovada contra a doença como parte do tal "tratamento". O vídeo está nas redes ao menos desde novembro de 2025 , e voltou a circular depois do debate entre os candidatos a presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nesta sexta-feira, na Globo , quando Lula mencionou o episódio. "Mais uma fake news que está caindo por terra. Como vocês viram, o presidente Bolsonaro jamais debochou das pessoas que estavam com falta de ar. A verdade é que ele estava denunciando o 'protocolo Mandetta', que recomendava as pessoas a procurarem os hospitais somente quando já estavam com falta de ar... Inclusive, o presidente sempre defendeu o tratamento precoce", diz uma mulher no vídeo , que circula no Facebook, no Instagram e no Threads. Flávio também postou o vídeo em seu Instagram como resposta à afirmação de Lula durante o debate de que Bolsonaro "apareceu na televisão rindo e imitando uma pessoa morrendo asfixiada", afirmando que o petista "mentiu" quando citou o episódio. As imagens do ex-presidente são de uma live transmitida em 18 de março de 2021. O vídeo checado critica a forma como a "mídia" teria retratado a imitação de Bolsonaro. Nos posts, Bolsonaro defende que pessoas com sintomas de Covid-19 procurem um médico imediatamente e afirma que "milhares de pessoas" se beneficiaram "desse tratamento inicial". Em seguida, as publicações mostram o trecho em que o ex-presidente ironiza a recomendação atribuída por ele ao ex-ministro da Saúde Luiz Henrique Mandetta e imita uma pessoa sem ar. No entanto, o corte não mostra o que Bolsonaro fala entre a recomendação de atendimento médico imediato e a menção aos supostos beneficiados pelo "tratamento inicial". "Alguns nem vão, já tomam logo o remédio pra matar piolho. Se falar o nome, também não pode. Eu tomei um outro, e me dei bem", disse . O "remédio para matar piolho" é a ivermectina, um vermífugo, e o que Bolsonaro disse ter tomado é a hidroxicloroquina . Ambos nunca tiveram eficácia comprovada contra a Covid-19 e não figuram entre os tratamentos recomendados pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS). É neste contexto que Bolsonaro afirma que "milhares de pessoas" se beneficiaram "desse tratamento inicial". Mais adiante, em outro trecho também omitido, o ex-presidente diz que quem fosse contra o tratamento sugerido por ele poderia seguir "a receita do ministro Mandetta". Em 2021, na CPI da Covid, o ex-ministro da Saúde negou que tivesse dado a orientação de aguardar o agravamento de sintomas para buscar atendimento médico. Procurada pela reportagem, a campanha de Flávio não respondeu a um pedido de comentário sobre a publicação do vídeo editado. VEREDICTO Enganoso. O vídeo omite que o "tratamento inicial" recomendado por Jair Bolsonaro era composto por medicamentos sem eficácia comprovada contra a Covid-19. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Lula, Bolsonaro rally supporters on final day before Brazil presidential runoff
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff vote, mobilizing supporters and making a final push for undecided voters.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso, Sebastian Rocandio, Lais Morais
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff vote, mobilizing supporters and making a final push for undecided voters. The two candidates have remained neck and neck in polls following a [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"stronger-than-expected"] performance by the right-wing senator in the first round. On Saturday, a [USN:S0N46101P TEXT:"CNT/MDA poll showed"] the senator with a 1.3-point lead. Lula, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, kicked off his last day of campaigning with a march along Rio de Janeiro's iconic Copacabana beach, where thousands of supporters joined the leftist incumbent under a blazing sun. "We're going to win the election for one simple reason: it's true that the people want change, (but) they want to move forward. They don't want to go backward," Lula told journalists before the rally. Later, the president led another march in Sao Paulo, passing along Paulista Avenue, a traditional venue for political demonstrations in Brazil's largest city. "It's so exciting to see everyone here. This is the kind of energy we want for Brazil. Brazil is ours," said Gisele Passos, a 61-year-old businesswoman at the Sao Paulo rally. For many Lula supporters, the rallies carried a bittersweet undertone. The 80-year-old president and former union leader is widely expected to be making his final bid for office, lending the campaign's closing events the feel of a farewell tour. "He's one of a kind. He has had an incredible, remarkable, and hard-fought journey. We're very proud of that," said Olga Leal, a 62-year-old retiree in Sao Paulo. BOLSONARO RALLIES IN BATTLEGROUND STATE Bolsonaro, meanwhile, joined a motorcycle caravan in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais, a key battleground state. No candidate has won the presidency without carrying Minas Gerais since the country's return to democracy in the 1980s. The senator led Lula by around 5 percentage points in the state in the first round. "The time is almost here. There are only a few hours left before we shape the future of our nation for the next 30 or 40 years," said the lawmaker, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, in a social media video. He later took part in a campaign march in his home state of Rio de Janeiro, which he has represented in the Senate since 2019. The younger Bolsonaro was first backed by his father to run for the presidency last December. The former president was sentenced to over 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula. On Friday, Lula and Bolsonaro met for a [USN:L1N46A011 TEXT:"final debate"] on TV Globo, the country's main free-to-air television channel, where they sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks.

item.title: Alvarez apologises for Barcelona comments after scoring Atletico winner
item.description: Julian Alvarez gave Atletico Madrid supporters a winning goal and an apology on Saturday, sealing a 1-0 victory over Deportivo La Coruna before seeking forgiveness for declaring his desire to play for Barcelona.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Julian Alvarez gave Atletico Madrid supporters a winning goal and an apology on Saturday, sealing a 1-0 victory over Deportivo La Coruna before seeking forgiveness for declaring his desire to play for Barcelona. The Argentine striker scored for the second successive match as Atletico moved within two points of LaLiga leaders Barca, then addressed the comments that had soured his relationship with fans at the Metropolitano. "I'd like to apologise to our fans for what I said at the World Cup; it was a mistake in terms of how I said it and the timing," Alvarez told Spanish broadcaster Movistar Plus. "I understand why the fans are angry. If I were a fan, I'd be angry too. Especially given how they've supported me since I arrived." Alvarez said during the 2026 World Cup that he "wanted to fulfil his dream" of playing for Barcelona, triggering a transfer dispute that stretched through pre-season and the summer window as [USN:L6N44O15D TEXT:"Atletico refused to sell "]to their rivals. Regularly booed at home this season, Alvarez received a standing ovation from some supporters after Saturday's goal. "I hope that with hard work and humility I can turn this situation around," he said. "I've been feeling better in recent matches – both physically and on the ball. I want to help the team and give my best." Second-placed Atletico have 25 points. Real Madrid, third with 21, visit Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday for the season's first Clasico.

item.title: Volkanovski keeps promise with quick win over Evloev at UFC 333
item.description: Australian Alexander Volkanovski retained his UFC featherweight title with a second-round technical knockout of Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 on Saturday, ending the Russian's unbeaten 20-fight professional run and keeping a promise to his wife.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australian Alexander Volkanovski retained his UFC featherweight title with a second-round technical knockout of Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 on Saturday, ending the Russian's unbeaten 20-fight professional run and keeping a promise to his wife. A thunderous combination sent Evloev backing up against the cage and Volkanovski followed him to the canvas before landing a series of unanswered blows that caused referee Marc Goddard to call off the fight with six seconds remaining in the frame. "It feels good to get a finish - I actually promised the missus, it was our wedding anniversary on Wednesday, I promised her a quick one so she wasn't stressing on the sideline, so there you go," he said grinning at his post-fight interview. The 38-year-old twice champion got through the first round without suffering too much damage and began to make his presence felt with precise striking in the second round, briefly sending Evloev to the canvas with a glancing blow to his temple. Evloev, 32, did his best to leverage his superior grappling but had no answer to Volkanovski's shrewd fighting style, which has been honed in a string of performances in title fights that have led pundits to consider him the best-ever featherweight. "I feel the love ... thank you so much. I really do appreciate it, I feel it from everyone, from the UFC staff, the fighters, every fan. The love that I get is just incredible, and I'm so thankful for it, so thank you all," he said. In the co-main event at The Etihad Arena on Yas Island, Russia's Petr Yan retained his bantamweight crown with a unanimous decision over Georgian Merab Dvalishvili in a battle fought at a frenetic pace from the first bell. The 33-year-old Yan, who took the belt from Dvalishvili by unanimous decision in December 2025, withstood a stream of takedown attempts and his piston-like punches left his opponent sporting several red welts on his face at the end of the fight. Facing Yan for the third time in his UFC career, Dvalishvili showed heart and courage, bouncing back repeatedly after shots to the body and head, but Yan kept his cool to pick him off, winning 48-47 on the scorecards of all three judges.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 51% dos votos válidos e Lula soma 49%, mostra Datafolha
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) conseguiu abrir uma vantagem numérica sobre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, ainda que os dois sigam em empate técnico, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) conseguiu abrir uma vantagem numérica sobre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, ainda que os dois sigam em empate técnico, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha neste sábado. Flávio tem 51% dos votos válidos contra 49% de Lula. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais para mais e para menos. Na sondagem anterior, divulgada na quinta-feira, os dois candidatos estavam numericamente empatados com 50% dos votos válidos, quando não são computados os votos brancos, nulos e os indecisos. No primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, Flávio terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Considerando as intenções de voto totais, a pesquisa mostra que Flávio soma 48% contra 47% de Lula. No levantamento anterior, era de 47% a 46% a favor de Flávio. Os que disseram que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum dos dois passaram a 3%, ante 5%, enquanto os indecisos se mantiveram em 2%. O Datafolha ouviu 4.050 eleitores entre sexta-feira e este sábado.

item.title: Inside the Trump-administration campaign to return Brazil’s Bolsonaro clan to power
item.description: Two US State Department officials led a campaign to restore the right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power in Brazil and successfully pushed for sanctions aimed at tilting the election in their favor, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Stargardter
item.content:encoded: Two US State Department officials led a campaign to restore the right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power in Brazil and successfully pushed for sanctions aimed at tilting the election in their favor, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter. Their plan faces a reckoning on Sunday, when Senator Flavio Bolsonaro faces leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a tight run-off. Lula has warned Washington against encroaching on Brazil's sovereignty and accused his opponent of plotting with the Trump administration. The two officials were Darren Beattie, a Senior Advisor for Western Hemisphere Affairs who [USN:L1N3ZM12Y TEXT:"oversees Brazil policy"], and Ricardo Pita, another senior advisor promoted this year to Deputy Assistant Secretary for North America. The details of their campaign to return the Bolsonaros to power haven't been previously reported. Beattie and Pita, both political appointees, operated with wide latitude to manage Washington's relationship with the second most-populous country in the Americas, the people said. In the months before election campaigning began, they instructed US diplomats in Brazil that it was US policy to restore former President Jair Bolsonaro as Brazil’s leader – even though he had been disqualified from office for plotting a coup in 2022, when he lost the presidential election to Lula, three of the people said. After Bolsonaro received a [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"27-year sentence in September 2025"], the two men pivoted to supporting the candidacy of his son, right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the three sources said. Beattie and Pita told embassy staff not to interact with other conservative presidential contenders who could challenge the younger Bolsonaro, they said. Since last year, the two men have successfully advocated for punitive US government measures on Brazil designed to weaken Lula and boost the Bolsonaros, the 10 people told Reuters. The policies included designating Brazilian gangs as terrorist groups and imposing US sanctions against the Brazilian Supreme Court Justice who was spearheading the investigation into Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters could not determine the extent to which the two men were acting on orders from the White House or Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Trump, a vocal defender of Bolsonaro since his election defeat in 2022, hasn’t publicly endorsed any candidate. The White House declined to comment and referred questions to the State Department. State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott didn't answer questions about specific measures and directives involving Beattie and Pita but said in a statement: "All actions taken by the United States against narco-traffickers and to protect free speech are to defend the rights and lives of the American people. The Brazilian people have the right to choose their leaders through free and fair elections." Lula’s office did not respond to comment requests. Orna Blum, one of the officials who spoke to Reuters about Beattie and Pita’s efforts, led the State Department's Brazil and Southern Cone office until retiring last year over her opposition to the Trump administration. Washington "has every right to pursue its economic and strategic interests," she said. "But when American foreign policy instruments are used to pressure another democracy over the legal fate of a political ally, the line between diplomacy and political intervention has been crossed." SANCTIONS ON A SUPREME COURT JUSTICE Beattie is a former White House speechwriter fired in 2018 after addressing an event frequented by white nationalists. He’s also the architect of " free speech diplomacy ," a policy advocated by Trump allies that seeks to punish nations they accuse of censoring right-wing speech by US citizens, companies and global right-wing allies. The United States has accused Brazil Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of violating free speech rights by jailing Brazilians for political social-media posts and by censoring content of US social-media companies. Moraes has argued he was ridding social media of fake news that undermined public faith in Brazil's democratic institutions. Moraes did not respond to a comment request. Pita, a conservative Venezuelan-American, is among many in Rubio's orbit who view Lula as a threat to US interests in Latin America. Rubio has been a key leader in the administration’s aggressive policy in the region, which has included an invasion of Venezuela to oust its president, an oil blockade of Cuba, and military attacks on suspected drug boats from Latin America. Beattie and Pita were drawn to the Bolsonaro family’s right-wing politics, their antipathy towards Lula, and the idea that Jair Bolsonaro was a victim of abuses by Brazil's Supreme Court. Like Trump in the 2020 US election, Bolsonaro refused to concede he lost Brazil’s 2022 presidential vote, triggering riots by supporters who stormed government buildings. The Supreme Court convicted him in September 2025 of plotting a coup to remain in power. Before the conviction, in early 2025, the Bolsonaros were aggressively lobbying Washington for sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act against Moraes, who had led criminal investigations into Jair Bolsonaro. The act is a 2016 federal law allowing US sanctions against foreign individuals responsible for human-rights abuses or severe corruption. Around April 2025, Jair Bolsonaro’s younger son, Eduardo, visited Beattie in his State Department office in Washington DC, according to two former US officials. Eduardo Bolsonaro had been making the public case for Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes since at least 2024, and in March 2025 he said in a livestream that it was "practically certain" the Trump administration would do so. Eduardo Bolsonaro did not respond to requests for comment. Beattie made calls to the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control to appeal for Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes, said a former US official with direct knowledge of the matter. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose department administers Magnitsky sanctions through OFAC, offered no opposition, the former official said. The US announced Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes in July 2025, citing his alleged violations of free-speech rights by censoring anti-government social-media posts. A Treasury official said Bessent and Rubio are "fully aligned on the administration’s foreign policy." TERRORIST DESIGNATIONS The Bolsonaro family was also pushing for Washington to designate Brazil's top gangs – the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) – as terrorist organizations. They believed such a designation would hurt Lula, who some opponents have criticized for failing to control crime. Eduardo Bolsonaro had become friends with Pita through US conservative circles, and both supported the effort to designate the gangs as terrorist groups. In May 2025, Pita joined a US delegation that visited Jair Bolsonaro at his residence in Brasilia as he awaited his trial, according to public announcements at the time. Also in the group: David Gamble, the State Department’s top sanctions official at the time. Back in Washington, Pita asked State sanctions officials to explore how terrorist designations like those [USN:S0N3ON011 TEXT:"announced against Mexican cartels"] in February 2025 could be used in Brazil, one former official said. Nearly a year later, in May 2026 – after Pita was promoted to a new job that pulled him out of Brazil affairs – presidential contender Flavio Bolsonaro met with Beattie and Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau in Washington to discuss "the urgency of designating the PCC and the Comando Vermelho as foreign terrorist organizations," according to an X post by right-wing influencer Paulo Figueiredo that included photos of the attendees. The State Department announced the designation the following day. Reuters could not determine the extent of Pita or Beattie’s influence in securing the final decision. BACKFIRES AND SETBACKS In July 2025, Washington also announced a series of other measures against Brazil, including the revocations of eight Supreme Court justices' visas and 50% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing the "persecution" of Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters could not determine what, if any, role Beattie or Pita played in the additional measures. But if they were intended to undermine Lula, many of them backfired, according to political analysts in Brazil. Measures targeting the court did nothing to stop it from proceeding with Bolsonaro's trial, while the tariffs boosted the Lula government's poll numbers, the analysts said. Major US and Brazilian firms reliant on bilateral trade – including meatpacking giant JBS (JBSS.O) - controlled by Brazilian billionaires Wesley and Joesley Batista – also pushed back on the tariffs, which Washington eventually watered down. Beattie and Pita’s campaign also hit setbacks. Without an official explanation from the Treasury Department, the US removed Justice Moraes from the Magnitsky sanctions list in December, and in March [USN:S0N3ZG01R TEXT:"Brazil barred Beattie"] from entering the country to visit Bolsonaro in prison. Mario Braga, a Latin America analyst at risk intelligence firm RANE, said Trump may have decided to withhold a public endorsement of Bolsonaro to avoid being seen as meddling in Brazil's election – a perception that could boost Lula’s popularity. Still, after Flavio Bolsonaro narrowly outperformed Lula in the first-round election earlier this month, Trump called it a big victory. "Close, but a very, very big victory," he told reporters. "Amazing, actually."

item.title: Lindt got chocolate price hikes wrong, chairman says after CEO's ouster
item.description: 'We overestimated how much we could raise prices without hurting demand.'
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lindt & Sprüngli (LISN.S) has struggled because it misjudged how consumers would respond to price increases, the chair of the Swiss chocolate maker said, days after the company [USN:L6N4650EX TEXT:"ousted"] its CEO over concerns about its performance. In an interview with the NZZ am Sonntag newspaper, Executive Chairman Ernst Tanner said the firm, whose shares have tumbled more than 25% this year after recent outlook [USN:L8N45L05W TEXT:"cuts"], was largely suffering because it had misread the market in Germany. "We misjudged how customers would respond to price increases. After cocoa prices reached historic highs from 2024 onwards, we wanted to pass on those additional costs. In doing so, we overestimated how much we could raise prices without hurting demand," he said. "For some consumers, our products clearly became too expensive in recent months." "Lindt & Sprüngli as a whole, however, is not in crisis," Tanner added, arguing the company's shares are now undervalued. "In the Americas and the Far East, we'll achieve our growth targets of 6% to 8% this year as well." Tanner, 80, who was CEO from 1993 to 2016 and has been chairman for over three decades, rejected the suggestion that he should stand down, saying he had important work to do to get Lindt back on track. "Once that's been achieved, I look forward to turning to the next phase of my life," he said. Tanner said the company had already cut some prices as it seeks to lift sales volumes, and would have more scope to do so once cocoa prices returned to more normal levels. He said there would not be group-wide job cuts and that the firm wanted to keep growing. Still, he said thrift was required and that bonuses would be affected in the Germany-Switzerland-Austria region as targets had been missed.

item.title: Bolsonaro y Lula reúnen a multitudes de seguidores antes de balotaje presidencial en Brasil
item.description: El senador Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva cerraron el sábado sus campañas para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, movilizando a multitudes de seguidores en un último esfuerzo por ganarse a los votantes indecisos en una contienda que aparece totalmente abierta.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso
item.content:encoded: El senador Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva cerraron el sábado sus campañas para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, movilizando a multitudes de seguidores en un último esfuerzo por ganarse a los votantes indecisos en una contienda que aparece totalmente abierta. Ambos candidatos aparecen prácticamente empatados en las encuestas de cara al balotaje del domingo tras un resultado mejor de lo esperado de Bolsonaro en la primera vuelta. Lula, que busca su cuarto mandato, comenzó su último día de campaña con una marcha por la playa de Copacabana, donde miles de simpatizantes se unieron al actual presidente bajo un sol abrasador. "Vamos a ganar las elecciones por una sencilla razón: es cierto que el pueblo quiere un cambio, y el pueblo quiere un cambio para mejor, el pueblo quiere avanzar. El pueblo no quiere dar marcha atrás", declaró Lula a periodistas antes del mitin. Más tarde, el presidente encabezó otra marcha en São Paulo, pasando por la Avenida Paulista, donde una multitud se reunió para mostrarle su apoyo. "Estoy emocionada. He venido en metro y ha sido muy emocionante ver a todo el mundo. Una energía que queremos para Brasil. Brasil es nuestro", dijo Gisele Passos, una empresaria de 61 años. Para muchos seguidores de Lula, los mítines tuvieron un tono agridulce. El presidente, de 80 años, se encuentra en su último intento por ser elegido, lo que dotó a los últimos actos de la campaña de un aire de despedida. "Es único. Tiene una trayectoria realmente maravillosa, increíble y llena de lucha. Estamos muy orgullosos de ello", afirmó Olga Leal, una jubilada de 62 años. Bolsonaro, por su parte, se unió a una caravana de motos en Belo Horizonte, con la mirada puesta en los votantes del crucial estado de Minas Gerais. Ningún candidato ha ganado la presidencia sin imponerse allí desde el retorno de la democracia al país en la década de 1980. "El momento está a punto de llegar. Quedan pocas horas para que cambiemos el destino de nuestra nación durante los próximos 30 o 40 años", afirmó el hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro en un video publicado en las redes sociales. Posteriormente participó en una marcha en Barra da Tijuca, en Río de Janeiro, frente al complejo residencial donde vivía su padre. Jair Bolsonaro se encuentra bajo arresto domiciliario en Brasilia tras haber sido condenado a más de 27 años de prisión por intento de golpe de Estado tras perder las elecciones de 2022 frente a Lula.

item.title: UK budget set to hand English mayors new borrowing powers, growth funding
item.description: British finance minister John Healey will use next week's budget to hand mayors in England new funding and powers, including a £1.5 billion ($2 billion) borrowing facility, as part of plans to move economic decision-making out of Westminster.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey will use next week's budget to hand mayors in England new funding and powers, including a £1.5 billion ($2 billion) borrowing facility, as part of plans to move economic decision-making out of Westminster. The measures include £285 million of seed funding next year under a new "Good Growth" scheme, which the finance ministry said would let local leaders invest in their own growth priorities without seeking permission from central government. "I'm calling time on local leaders going cap in hand to Westminster. That is no way to run a country," said Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Here are the key points: • The Good Growth funding is designed to reduce local leaders' reliance on fragmented bidding pots from central government • The funds can be used for housing, regenerating high streets and improving transport links • The government will work with mayors to design the £1.5 billion borrowing facility, which it said would give them access to capital to back local growth projects • Strategic authorities will receive a further £150 million next year to build up staff and expertise as they take on bigger budgets ($1 = 0.7478 pounds)

item.title: Trump announces Audi will build $4 billion US factory in Georgia
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that Audi plans to build a $4 billion assembly plant in Georgia that will produce 200,000 SUVs annually, as he seeks to convince Americans to back Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that Audi plans to build a $4 billion assembly plant in Georgia that will produce 200,000 SUVs annually, as he seeks to convince Americans to back Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections. Trump, who has pressured automakers to move production to the United States and has raised tariffs on autos, steel, aluminum and parts, made the announcement at a rally in Perry, near Macon in central Georgia, where Volkswagen's (VOWG.DE) premium subsidiary intends to build its first US assembly plant. Last year, Trump's tariffs dealt Audi a €1.2-billion-euro ($1.4-billion) blow as it imports all its vehicles for the US market from Europe or Mexico. Georgia has competitive election races for US Senate and governor. Trump is eager to make the case that his auto tariffs are helping the US economy. Critics say they have boosted vehicle prices and that the trade uncertainty has delayed some automaker investments. "We are planning to bring our biggest and most premium SUVs, and produce them here in Macon, Georgia," Audi CEO Gernot Doellner said at the event. "This is a this is a long-term investment because we believe in the American market." REPUBLICAN SAYS TARIFFS BROUGHT AUDI PLANT TO UNITED STATES Audi said the investment will create approximately 4,500 jobs. Construction is scheduled to begin next year, with production starting in the early 2030s, Audi said. The plant is expected to assemble the Audi Q7, Q8 and Q9 SUVs, a US official told Reuters. Audi also plans to build 25,000 vehicles a year in neighboring South Carolina, the official said. Some of the vehicles, now built in Europe, would be exported, the official added. Those vehicles will be assembled at a $2 billion plant of VW's off-road brand Scout Motors that is under construction in Blythewood, near the state capital, Columbia, the official said. Trump has cut government incentives for electric vehicles, causing a significant reduction in US EV and battery production. US vehicle and parts employment has fallen since Trump took office last year. A gold Audi with manufacturer license plates was parked outside Trump's rally. US Senator Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican, said late on Saturday that "with this investment, Audi will build all of their SUVs exclusively in the US." He said the Audi plant "would never have happened without tariffs, without common sense regulations and without eliminating California’s ability to regulate fuel economy standards." Audi sales have fallen for two consecutive years and slid 7% in the first half of 2026 as fierce competition in China and US tariffs hit demand. Audi's US sales are down 16% this year. Audi's Neckarsulm plant in southwest Germany is one of four German Volkswagen plants facing possible closure after 2030. In July, Japan's Toyota said it would spend $3.6 billion to build a 2.5-million-square-foot (232,000-square-metre) truck assembly line on its San Antonio, Texas, manufacturing campus and shift some truck production to the US from Mexico. The Japanese automaker said the expansion would be completed by 2030, creating 2,000 jobs. Honda Motor (7267.T) is considering building a US assembly plant but has warned it may not unless the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement on trade is extended. South Korea's Hyundai said last year that if it had certainty about USMCA, it "would immediately unlock over $20 billion in new American investments."

item.title: Flávio tem 50,5% dos votos válidos e Lula soma 49,5%, mostra pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico, com vantagem numérica do senador sobre o presidente, mostrou pesquisa BTG/Nexus divulgada neste sábado, véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico, com vantagem numérica do senador sobre o presidente, mostrou pesquisa BTG/Nexus divulgada neste sábado, véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial. Flávio tem 50,5% dos votos válidos, quando não são computados os votos brancos, nulos e os indecisos, contra 49,5% de Lula. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2,2 pontos percentuais para mais e para menos. No primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, Flávio terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Considerando as intenções de voto totais, o senador soma 47% contra 46% do presidente, segundo a pesquisa deste sábado. No levantamento anterior, no início da semana, o placar era de 46,5% a 45,9% a favor de Flávio. Os que disseram que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum dos dois passaram a 5,2%, ante 4,7%, enquanto os indecisos foram a 1,8%, ante 2,9%. A Nexus ouviu 2.000 eleitores entre sexta-feira e este sábado.

item.title: China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs
item.description: Beijing said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties with the United States.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs

Beijing said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties with the United States.

BEIJING: The Chinese commerce ministry urged the United States on Saturday (Oct 24) to stop expanding restrictions on American investments in China , saying a proposed rule on sensitive technologies would disrupt trade ties. The US Treasury Department issued proposals on Thursday to update its outbound-investment security programme , adding biotechnology to restricted sectors and expanding coverage of high-performance computing and hypersonic systems. Beijing's commerce ministry said in a statement that the proposal "discriminatorily" widened China -related investment restrictions and intensified curbs. It firmly opposed the US proposal and reserved the right to take unspecified countermeasures, it added. Beijing also said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties and ran counter to the consensus reached by the countries' presidents, who have met twice in the past six months. The US Treasury has said the measures, which do not only cover China , are intended to stop US capital from supporting foreign adversaries' development of dual-use strategic technologies that could threaten US national security. The US programme had already restricted certain US investments involving China in semiconductors, quantum technologies and artificial intelligence.
